Read more: Mark Zuckerberg on new audio glasses, Muse and if AI will kill us all
Video: Watch the full interview with Mark Zuckerberg
Mark Zuckerberg says Meta will lead on smart glasses privacy despite ‘pervert glasses’ criticism
Video: Zuckerberg shows Meta's audio-only glasses, addresses safety concerns
Several AI companies — including Amazon and Nvidia — have also released their own AI agents since the first widespread consumer-facing agent, OpenClaw, burst onto the AI scene in November.
As an example of Muse’s capabilities, Zuckerberg said his own Muse agent helped give feedback on his mixed martial arts performance by connecting to cameras watching over his workout area.
“You’re basically going to have an extremely capable assistant who can understand the things that you care about,” Zuckerberg said.

Rather than worry about distant apocalyptic scenarios from rapidly improving AI systems, Zuckerberg said, AI companies should focus on making sure their systems understand users’ desires and intents and handle that information with discretion.
“Nailing those things are going to be the most important next things to align with what people actually want in the world,” Zuckerberg said.

Zuckerberg pointed out that the Muse system is actually several agents working together — another Meta AI agent, called Sentinel, oversees and polices the main Muse agent. If the Sentinel observes the Muse agent potentially exceeding its remit, the oversight agent can alert users and ask for human permission before carrying out any further actions.

“The AI agent needs to be trained from the ground up to have a sense of what information is OK to share and what isn’t,” Zuckerberg said. Muse and other AI agents have stoked privacy concerns, given the amount of information and access that users can provide to them, including linking email accounts, bank cards and more so they can act without human intervention.
Zuckerberg said users’ information was safe with Meta, pointing to the company’s track record on privacy and WhatsApp’s encrypted messaging as evidence that users could trust Muse with their data.

“We’ve shown that we have the ability to build those kinds of world-class, leading security systems,” Zuckerberg said, mentioning that Meta worked with a field-leading cryptographer behind the popular anonymous Signal messaging app to develop its own secure technology. “I think that’s something that people can feel very good about.”

Taking stock of the larger AI landscape, Zuckerberg distanced himself from warnings from Coxon and other researchers that AI could cause human extinction within a few years. Instead, he highlighted how personalized AI systems could revolutionize human life — echoing his August essay about the dawn of personalized superintelligence.
“There’s a lot of rhetoric that is filled with doom,” Zuckerberg said. “I’m quite optimistic about the fact that this is going to be a very positive future for everyone.”

title: Netanyahu takes the U.N. stage facing global isolation and a fight for his political future
summary: As Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case at the United Nations General Assembly, his target audience will likely be Israeli voters.
story: TEL AVIV — Even as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case to the world at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, his target audience will likely be closer to home: Israeli voters ahead of next month’s crucial elections.
Netanyahu arrived in New York Thursday for what appears to be a whirlwind trip that will highlight the growing isolation of the U.S. ally over its assault on the Gaza Strip.

With only a handful of diplomatic meetings on the sidelines of the assembly and President Donald Trump’s focus firmly on his summit with China’s Xi Jinping, the prime minister looks set to return to Israel shortly after his address to be back in time for the major Jewish Sukkot holiday on Friday evening.

“I am leaving tonight for New York in order to defend, from the U.N. podium, Israel and IDF soldiers,” the prime minister said in a video Wednesday night before he left. “You hear the terrible lies that are being spread there.”

Netanyahu is likely to address an almost empty chamber as delegates observe an annual tradition of walking out in protest over the conduct of Israel’s war in the Gaza Strip. But that spectacle will likely play well among the premier’s domestic supporters, for whom he has styled himself as a defiant truth-teller standing up for Israel on the global stage.

While much of the world has condemned Israel for the huge loss of civilian life and continuing humanitarian tragedy in Gaza, Netanyahu’s primary domestic challenge comes from an Israeli right-wing who accuses him of not being tough enough in the country’s multi-front war on Iran and its proxy groups.

“The main reason that brings him to the UN General Assembly this time is the opportunity to talk, using the UN microphone, to his voters in Israel, in his polished English, in a speech that of course will be accompanied by exaggerated descriptions of his great achievements,” wrote Efraim Ganor, a political, a strategic affairs expert, wrote in the right-leaning Israeli newspaper Ma’ariv.
The few hints that Netanyahu has given about the subject of his speech have focused on populist, patriotic causes.

In a video posted to social media on Tuesday, Netanyahu took aim at a popular target: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who had pledged to arrest him for crimes against humanity before later acknowledging that he lacked the jurisdiction to do so.

Appearing to adopt the posture of a professional wrestler and looking straight into the camera, Netanyahu accused the mayor of supporting Hamas — which Mamdani has strenuously denied — and fomenting riots against New York Jews. He added that he would  “tell the truth about you” and “tell the truth about our heroic soldiers.”
Asked about his comments, Mamdani told a news conference Tuesday that the Israeli military had killed an 11-year-old boy in a zone deemed safe in Gaza, “so that is what I have to say to his video.”

Netanyahu’s mention of Israel soldiers appears to be a reference to “NAZA,” a documentary made by two Israeli filmmakers in which 24 anonymous Israelis, described as military and intelligence officials, talk about the cynical process by which the country’s military evaluated the need for civilian deaths during the Gaza war.
A popular target that has riled Israeli leaders ahead of the elections, “NAZA” has earned plaudits abroad but condemnation at home.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Politicians have stumbled over themselves to publicly condemn the documentary in the harshest terms, with some demanding a criminal investigation into the duo and even stripping them of Israeli citizenship.
In another hint on Wednesday night, Netanyahu, who has a history of peppering his general assembly speeches with props, gags and gimmicks, said his speech would include “surprises.”
Last year, he told the audience that his speech was being broadcast into Gaza through massive loudspeakers and streamed to mobile phones so that Israeli hostages trapped in Gaza could hear him speak.

He also wore an oversized QR code on his jacket, encouraging audiences to activate the code to visit a website with a video showing Hamas’s attacks on Israel in October 2023 that killed about 1,200 people and sparked the latest round of fighting. Israel’s subsequent war in Gaza killed more than 75,000 people, according to Palestinian health official

In the years before that, Netanyahu brandished regional maps to make his points. Two years ago, he displayed two maps that showed the “blessing” of Israel’s influence contrasted with the “curse” of Iran’s expanding power.

And in 2012, more than a decade before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in what they said was an attempt to keep the Islamic Republic from getting a nuclear weapon, Netanyahu held up a cartoon image of an Iranian nuclear weapon with a “red line” for its maximum enrichment level.

title: Trump’s FDA pick to face scrutiny over abortion pill access at confirmation hearing
summary: Dr. Heidi Overton is also expected to address President Donald Trump’s claim labeling the measles vaccine “lethal.”
story: Dr. Heidi Overton, a fierce opponent of abortion rights, is set to appear before senators Thursday for her confirmation hearing to lead the Food and Drug Administration.

The hearing before the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee comes as the FDA faces pressure from Republicans, including the committee’s chair, Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., to tighten access to the abortion pill mifepristone.

Cassidy, who is a key vote in Overton’s confirmation, has been pushing the administration to reverse a Biden-era rule that allows mifepristone to be prescribed via telemedicine and sent through the mail.

In a committee report published last month, Cassidy accused the makers of mifepristone of failing to meet their legal responsibilities to ensure compliance with FDA safety regulations, particularly when the pills are sold online through third-party providers. At a hearing in January, Cassidy called on Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the previous FDA commissioner, Dr. Marty Makary, to complete a safety review that they both promised during their confirmation hearings. In June, the FDA said it launched a new safety study on mifepristone.
Art Caplan, the head of the medical ethics division at NYU Grossman School of Medicine in New York City, said Overton’s views on abortion appear to align with Cassidy’s.

Overton, a preventive medicine physician, currently serves as a domestic policy official in the White House. Prior to that, she worked as chief policy officer at the conservative think tank America First Policy Institute, where she praised the Supreme Court’s decision overturning Roe v. Wade and called for strict restrictions on medication abortion, claiming that it is “dangerous to women.” (Studies have shown that the drug, even when taken at home, is safe and effective.)

If confirmed, Overton would take over an agency that has been without a permanent commissioner since Makary resigned in May, in part over the administration’s decision to authorize several fruit-flavored vapes for adults.

As commissioner, Overton would serve as a key ally to Kennedy, whose department oversees the FDA. Overton is a proponent of Kennedy’s “Make America Healthy Again” movement. She also appeared alongside President Donald Trump in August when he announced an executive order aimed at reducing the number of vaccines routinely recommended for children. Trump nominated her to lead the agency days later.
Senators are likely to grill her about her own views on vaccines, according to Dorit Reiss, a professor of law and vaccine policy expert at the University of California Law San Francisco.

On CBS News’ “Face the Nation” on Sunday, Cassidy — who has also aggressively questioned and pressed several Trump administration nominees on vaccines — said Overton must acknowledge that Trump’s claim that the measles vaccine is lethal is “absurd” when she appears before his committee. Trump made the comment during the August signing of his vaccine executive order.

“I think she made it clear she’s a supporter of Kennedy’s vaccine agenda, at least,” Reiss said. “Dr. Overton seems like another example of an appointee who is, primarily, appointed for political opinions, without an emphasis on qualifications.”
Overton, Reiss said, doesn’t appear to have expertise in clinical trials, managing an agency or any of the products the FDA regulates.

“It’s reasonable for an administration to want someone sympathetic to their views,” Reiss said, “but FDA commissioner is a hard job that requires the ability to manage a large and complex agency that does important work.”

“As an MD/PhD who helped President Trump deliver on Operation Warp Speed during his first term, Dr. Heidi Overton will ensure that policymaking is guided solely by Gold Standard Science at the FDA,” White House spokesman Kush Desai said in a statement.
Dr. Stephen Ostroff, a former acting FDA commissioner, said food safety will be another major issue waiting for her at the FDA.

The agency has spent much of the summer responding to a series of foodborne illness outbreaks and recalls, including a massive cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce that sickened more than 12,000 people across multiple states.

The outbreak has also raised questions about how quickly the FDA can trace contaminated food back to its source and whether the agency has enough staff to respond to outbreaks after thousands of employees left or were laid off over the past year.

“After the experience of the past 18 months, it’s very important to restore public and industry confidence that decisions being made by FDA, including those by leadership, are science-based, transparent and consistent,” Ostroff said.

title: Judge orders White House to restore access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico
summary: A federal judge ordered early Thursday that the White House immediately restore access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico, saying that President Donald Trump’s directive barring the three news outlets was most likely unconstitutional.
story: A federal judge early Thursday ordered that the White House immediately restore access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico for the time being, saying that President Donald Trump’s directive barring the three news outlets was most likely unconstitutional.

In granting a 14-day temporary restraining order reinstating the outlets’ access while their legal challenge proceeds, U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly wrote that the plaintiffs are likely to succeed in their lawsuit against the Trump administration, at least on the grounds that their credentials were revoked last week without due process.
Trump, he wrote, did not dispute that the outlets “did not receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before their hard passes were revoked.”
The White House did not respond to a request for overnight comment from NBC News.

“This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action,” the attorney representing the news outlets, Ted Boutrous, said in a statement.

The three news outlets reported that their employees had been denied access to the White House grounds early Thursday, though it was not immediately clear whether that was a result of a technical issue or the administration failing to comply with the judge’s order.

Trump had posted on social media before a Wednesday hearing in the case that he expected the “totally disloyal” Kelly, whom he nominated to the bench during his first term, to rule against him — adding that “as usual, we’ll go for appeal.”
Inside lawsuit challenging Trump's White House outlet ban
Trump announced the ban on the three news outlets in a post on Truth Social on Friday, saying it was “a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow,” he said.
Thursday’s order rejected the White House’s argument that banning the outlets was motivated by national security concerns, saying it offered little proof to back up the claim.

“Certainly, that is not what President Trump said when he announced that he was ‘banning’ Plaintiffs from the White House — instead, he focused on the alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity of Plaintiffs’ reporting,” Kelly wrote.
Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office a short time after the post, Trump referred to his directive as “the ban on the free press.”
“I don’t want them in my office. I don’t want them here,” he said.
He said the policy was not in response to a particular report, but because of “cumulative stories over the last few years.”

“They purposely write negative news. And they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration,” he said. “If they could straighten themselves out, I’d love it,” he added.

The outlets said in their suit challenging the ban that Trump’s remarks show the policy was motivated by “retaliation” and “intended to cow” the outlets “into changing their reporting and threaten other journalists lest they suffer the same fate.”

The “Constitution does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on that official’s dislike of the content of their reporting. The ban is patently unconstitutional and should be immediately restrained,” they argued.

The White House appeared to be trying to address those due process claims in letters to the news outlets on Tuesday, which told them they could “contest this initial decision” in written responses by Friday.
The letters accuse them of publishing “sensitive security information, and misinformation” which “undermines the President’s ability to safeguard the national security.”

title: Yemen says it asked Trump for U.S. military support in fight against Houthis
summary: A senior official said Yemen is seeking help as the Iranian-backed rebels tighten their grip on its Red Sea coast, threatening to further disrupt global energy shipments.
story: The government of Yemen is seeking U.S. military support in its fight against the Houthis, a senior Yemeni official said Wednesday, as the Iranian-backed rebels rapidly expand their control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and threaten another critical Middle East waterway for global energy supplies.

Yemen’s president, Rashad al-Alimi, conveyed the request for U.S. assistance to President Donald Trump in a call this week, Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, vice president of the Yemeni Leadership Council, told reporters on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly.

Asked about a report this week by Reuters, which cited one Yemeni and one Western source as saying Trump made no direct pledge of military support during the call, Bawazir said he was unaware that the request had been rejected.
He said that Trump understands the danger of the Houthis and that “we hope and expect more support for the Yemeni government in the face of the Houthi militias.”
The White House did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment overnight.
Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
Bawazir did not say whether U.S. support should extend to direct military strikes.
“We do not ask the American soldiers to actually go into war on our behalf,” he said. “And we don’t really request that they do nothing.”

Yemen does look forward to “mutual coordination on the intel and security fields,” according to Bawazir, who requested that the U.S. enhance the Yemeni government’s own military capacity to take on the threat.
“The aerial campaigns are important,” he said. “But supporting the Yemeni government and forces on the ground is indeed a guarantor to end the danger of those militias.”

Yemen has been embroiled in various states of conflict since 2014, when the Houthis drove the internationally recognized government out of the capital city, Sanaa, and ignited a regional proxy war, with Saudi Arabia supporting the exiled government against the Iranian-backed rebels.

In their latest military campaign, the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline with the aim of cutting off the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which has become a critical waterway for Saudi Arabia to transport oil after Iran effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia, a critical U.S. ally in the Middle East, including in the U.S. war with Iran, has urged the U.S. to take military action against the Houthis, who further escalated their actions over the weekend by launching an attack on the Saudi capital, Riyadh. So far U.S. support has been limited to providing intelligence and targeting data.

Trump, who announced a ceasefire with the Houthis last year after weeks of punishing strikes against the militant group, went so far as to order strikes against the Houthis on Sunday, NBC News has reported, but the order was canceled hours later.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that the U.S. has made commitments to the Saudis and is living up to them, adding that “obviously, the president has many options available to him.”
Trump said this month that the Houthis, which the U.S. designates as a terrorist organization, don’t want to fight the U.S. and “they don’t want us to go after them.”

“They’ve called and they’ve talked to us, and they don’t want us to,” Trump told reporters while he was in Ireland. “They would much prefer not having us involved, and they’re letting most ships go through.”

Mohamed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, told The Associated Press on Sunday that it was the U.S. that had reached out to the rebel group after its advancement toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
“We confirmed that we are not targeting the United States, or any other nation, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy,” al-Bukhaiti said. “And that remains the case.”

Bawazir warned it would be a mistake to accept assurances from a group that is “connected to a deviant state in the region,” referring to Iran, as it may be seen as legitimizing the Houthis. But he said Yemen was comfortable with the U.S. position.
“We do indeed discuss this particular issue very, very deeply,” he said.

title: 8 service members attempted suicide on the USS Lincoln during extended deployment, Navy says
summary: The ship, which supported the U.S. war with Iran, was at sea for nearly 300 days without a port call.
story: Eight Navy members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have attempted suicide since the beginning of their extended deployment, a top Navy official said in a letter obtained by NBC News.

The length of the deployment, which some service members on board the carrier had described as extraordinarily tough, has raised concerns about supply shortages and the effect on sailors’ mental health.
No deaths have been attributed to suicide during the deployment.

The number of suicide attempts includes those by crewmembers and sailors from the carrier air wing, strike group and destroyer squadron staff; escorting destroyers; and all embarked aviation squadrons, according to the letter, which acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao sent to Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y.
About 7,500 service members, primarily sailors, are part of the strike group.
A Navy official said the letter was delivered to Gillibrand on Tuesday.

The official said the number of sailors who jumped overboard while the Lincoln was in the Middle East providing operations for the war in Iran remains at two, as previously reported. The official did not provide details about the six other attempts.
In the letter, Cao answered a series of questions that Gillibrand, a member of the Armed Services Committee, had asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in a previous letter.
The letter also addressed Gillibrand’s concerns about conditions and medical resources aboard the Lincoln.
In a statement, Gillibrand said the conditions on the ship were “serious and deteriorating.”
“Our troops and their families make immense sacrifices every single day, yet the president dismissed them with open disrespect,” she said.
President Donald Trump has previously said the deployment was “not nearly long enough.”
The ship was at sea without a port call for 286 days supporting the U.S. war with Iran. A typical deployment is six to seven months, with regular stops to replenish food supplies.

The Lincoln left San Diego in November. Its deployment was supposed to end in May, but it was extended after the war began in February. The ship stopped in Thailand this month and is now sailing back to San Diego after a stop in Guam.

Relatives of those on board raised concerns about food shortages and low morale and how the extended time at sea was “wreaking havoc” on sailors’ mental health, as one relative described it to NBC News last month.

Some military officials have played down or rejected those claims. In an op-ed in The Wall Street Journal last month, Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of U.S. Central Command, described the concerns as “old news” that were resolved months ago.
This summer, a Navy official said that officials had not observed an increase in suicidal ideations or attempts aboard the ship and that service members’ well-being was a top priority.

“We take every service member’s well-being seriously and have religious, medical and mental health professionals available to assess and address concerns as they arise,” the official said in a statement.

The Lincoln has five chaplains, a clinical psychologist, a clinical social worker, behavioral health technicians and an embedded integrated prevention coordination counselor to support the crew, the Navy official said.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Walmart Deal Days sale is happening at the same time as fall Prime Day — here’s everything you should know
summary: Walmart’s Deal Day sale event is returning from Oct. 5 to 11. The sale will happen at the same time as Prime Big Deal Days, also known as October Prime Day, and will include sales on beauty products, TVs, holiday gifts and more.
story: Of all the sales Walmart has throughout the year, the most important ones happen in the summer and fall. In fact, this October, the retailer’s annual fall sale, Walmart Deal Days, is returning this year and will take place Oct. 5 to 11. The sale will overlap with Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, also referred to as October Prime Day or fall Prime, which is happening Oct. 6 and 7.

Walmart’s Deal Days sale will have up to 50% off home, kitchen, tech, skin care, toys and video games, entertainment, electronics and more. You’ll also find markdowns on brands like Apple, Dyson, Shark, Ninja, Beautiful by Drew Barrymore, Revlon, Coach, Mainstays, Samsung and many more. So if you’re shopping for a new television set, air fryer, bedding, hair care tool or holiday gifts ahead of Thanksgiving and Christmas, this is a great opportunity to do it. Even food items will be up to 30% off.
Below, I talk more about the Walmart Deal Days sale, including whether or not you need a Walmart+ membership to shop the sale.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
When is Walmart’s October Deal Days sale?

Walmart’s Deal Days sale 2026 is happening Oct. 5 to 11, which overlaps with Amazon’s annual October Prime Day, which will take place Oct. 6 and 7. The Walmart deals will officially be live at 12 a.m. ET.
Do you need a membership to shop deals from Walmart’s Deal Days sale?

No, you don’t need a Walmart membership to shop deals from Walmart’s Deal Days sale. Though, those with a Walmart + membership typically get advanced access its sales, according to Walmart. A Walmart+ membership costs $12.95 a month ($98 a year), plus taxes.

Best early deals from Walmart’s Deal Days sale

Apple AirPods 4

Apple AirPods 4 are loved by NBC Selected staffers and have some of the best sound quality of all the earbuds we’ve tested. They get up to 30 hours of total listening time (with the USB-C charging case included). The earbuds also have voice isolation, which helps lower environmental sounds to make it easier for you to hear during phone calls and for the person you’re talking to hear you more clearly. They have spatial audio, which means your music, podcasts and audiobooks have immersive, 3D-like sound. Both the case and the AirPods themselves are water, dust and sweat resistant.

As a home and kitchen editor and someone who cooks a lot myself, Beautiful by Drew Barrymore is one of my favorite kitchen appliance brands. This particular appliance is a mix between a stovetop skillet and an electric hot plate. It’s great for sautéing vegetables, making stir fries, searing meat and poultry and anything else you’d cook in a skillet. It comes with a glass lid (allowing you to watch your food and prevent burning) and it also has a holder for the lid, which helps you avoid dripping food or condensation on your countertop.

This set of stainless steel mixing bowls includes five bowls of increasing size, each of which comes with a lid. Perfect for marinating, baking and meal prepping, the bowls are also freezer safe and rust resistant, and since they’re made of stainless steel, they won’t break if you drop them on the floor or table. They’re also dishwasher safe so cleaning is simple. And, since they increase in size, they’re all nestable, which helps save room in your cabinets.

I’ve written a lot about vacuums as an editor that covers cleaning and home products, and iRobot is one of the best robot vacuum brands available. This model is both a vacuum and mop that uses Lidar mapping technology, which allows it to learn your home to provide an efficient cleaning process and avoid running into furniture. It contains niacinamide, which is known to soothe skin, and ceramides and shea butter, both of which supply moisture, all without leaving behind a greasy feel.

title: How to store your air conditioner for the winter
summary: Removing your air conditioner from the window for winter can help prevent freezing temperatures and excess moisture from ruining it. HVAC experts share exactly how you should store it.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like whether jazz shoes are bad for your feet.

Fall has officially arrived, and with the cooler air (in most states) comes a fresh round of seasonal chores. Outdoor furniture gets covered up, sweaters come out of storage, and your window air conditioner needs to come out of the window. If that last task isn’t on your list, it should be.

According to Josh Mitchell, an HVAC technician and owner of Air Conditioner Lab, a site that helps consumers get information on HVAC issues, leaving your unit in place all winter can shorten its lifespan. But simply yanking it out and tucking it into a closet isn’t the answer either. Cleaning it and storing it the right way, Mitchell says, helps ensure it’s ready to perform when hot weather returns.
To help you take down, clean and store your air conditioner properly, I asked HVAC experts for their best advice. Here’s what they recommend.
When should you put your air conditioner in storage?

There’s no single right date for storing your AC unit; hot sleepers may want to hang on to theirs  a little longer, while those who get chilly at night may be ready to take it out sooner. Still, there’s a good benchmark you can follow.

“The general rule is that when the outdoor temperature continuously falls below 60 degrees Fahrenheit, you know it is time to turn off your air conditioner,” says Ben Green, an associate at The Chill Brothers, an HVAC service company in Texas. “You probably will not need the air conditioning once it gets that cool, and keeping it on could allow chilly drafts to enter your house.” Don’t wait for the first frost, either, Green adds, since freezing temperatures can damage the unit.
How to remove your air conditioner
Window air conditioners are bulky, heavy and awkward to maneuver, so taking one out can be a challenge. Once the unit is unplugged, these steps from Green can help make the job go more smoothly:

Remove the seals and weather stripping. Anything you used to keep the unit snug in the window can make it stick when you try to pull it out.Take off the brackets. Unscrew or unclip anything holding the unit in place.Tilt it slightly inward. As you lift it, angling the unit toward the room keeps leftover water from splashing back into your home.Watch the frame and sill. Lift carefully so the unit doesn’t bang into either one, which can cause damage to your AC and the window it’s in.Set it on a towel. Any remaining water will drip out, so let the towel catch it.
Remove the seals and weather stripping. Anything you used to keep the unit snug in the window can make it stick when you try to pull it out.
Take off the brackets. Unscrew or unclip anything holding the unit in place.
Tilt it slightly inward. As you lift it, angling the unit toward the room keeps leftover water from splashing back into your home.
Watch the frame and sill. Lift carefully so the unit doesn’t bang into either one, which can cause damage to your AC and the window it’s in.
Set it on a towel. Any remaining water will drip out, so let the towel catch it.
What products can you use to clean an air conditioner?

Below I share some tips on how to clean your air conditioner before you store it, so you’ll want to gather some of these cleaning supplies before you dive into the process. While you can certainly use a damp cloth and some soap and water, the experts I spoke with say there are also a handful of products on the market that can help you get the job done.
Mr.Siga Microfiber Cleaning Cloth
ReusableHold up after many washesDon’t leave streaks or lint

Each cloth is machine washable, so it holds up to repeated use. The color-coded pack makes it easy to keep one cloth for your air conditioner and others for other jobs.

NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans has them and she says she uses them to clean so many things around the home. “I wipe the dust from my air vents and furniture with these, not to mention they’re great for washing dishes and wiping windows and mirrors without leaving streaks and lint on glass,” she says.

It’s worth noting that while some dirt may come off if you use the brushes dry, using a bit of soap and water or a coil cleaner in conjunction with the brushes will allow them to be most effective.
How to clean your air conditioner before storing it

Once the unit is out of the window, give it a good cleaning before it goes into storage. It’s a key step for two reasons. “Dust and debris left on your air conditioner can reduce its efficiency when you go to restart it in the summer,” says Green. “Plus, if you put your AC away with water in it, mold could grow and nobody wants to inhale that when you turn it back on.”

The good news is that the job is relatively easy. “Simply wipe down the outside of it well and remember to clean or change the air filter,” says Green. If you see dirt on the coils, he adds, you can vacuum them or clean them lightly. Mitchell recommends washing the filter with a mild solution of soap and water. You can also use the products we mention above to ensure a thorough cleaning.
Finally, make sure everything is completely dry before you pack the unit away. Wipe down any spots that look damp, then let it sit in a cool, dry place until you’re certain no moisture remains.
How to store your air conditioner

Your AC is out of the window and clean, which means it’s finally ready to go into hibernation until warm weather returns. If you still have the original box, that’s the best place for it, says Green. No box? Wrap the unit in plastic instead. Either way, you’ll keep out dampness, dust and critters, he adds. Just make sure the unit sits upright, the same way it does in a window. “This is crucial because any residual fluids from tipping it could damage interior compartments,” says Green.

Next comes choosing the right spot. “Select a location that is dry and away from very hot or cold temperatures,” says Mitchell. “A garage, cellar, or even a closet are the ideal spaces. Just stay away from sheds and attics that could get extremely damp or cold in the winter. The worst thing for your unit is moisture, as it can cause rust and electrical damage.”

title: Sunny Hostin reveals she was holdout juror in 1991 ‘Butcher of Tompkins Square Park’ trial
summary: Hostin said on “The View” that she changed her fellow jurors’ minds to find Daniel Rakowitz not criminally responsible by reason of insanity at his 1991 New York City trial.
story: “The View” host Sunny Hostin revealed that she was the holdout juror in the high-profile “Butcher of Tompkins Square Park” trial in 1991.
Hostin spoke about her time serving on that jury during a discussion about the Lindsay Clancy case, which ended this month in a mistrial with the jury split 11-1.

“The reason I felt that I feel so strongly about this holdout juror is because I was a holdout juror in a case, in the Daniel Rakowitz case,” Hostin said on Tuesday’s episode, to the shock of her castmates.

Rakowitz was accused of killing and dismembering Monika Beerle, a 26-year-old dance student, then boiling her body parts and feeding them in a soup to people in Tompkins Square Park in the East Village of Manhattan in 1989.
He was found not guilty by reason of insanity at his 1991 trial, which dominated headlines.
Hostin said she served on the jury before she went to law school.
“When I brought it up at the Hot Topics meeting, I don’t think everyone believed me. And then my producer looked it up, and I’m in The New York Times,” she said.

The show then aired a picture of a newspaper clipping from an old New York Times article that read: “Several jurors questioned afterward said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict.”

“That was me,” Hostin said. “It was because I saw clearly that he was psychotic. He was in psychosis. He did not mean to kill her, and once he killed her, he panicked. He chopped up her body parts. Yes, boiled her body parts. Tried to commit the perfect crime ... and he fed her body parts to the unhoused.”
The jury deliberated for an intense nine days, and its talks were at times combative, Hostin recalled.

“One juror threw a chair at me they were so angry with me. But one by one I picked them off and said: ‘What about this? What about that?’ And we ended up all 12 unanimously voting that he was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity,” she said.
Rakowitz was ordered in 2010 to remain at maximum-security Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center on Ward’s Island.
Hostin noted that Rakowitz remains in a mental institution, which she called “a different type of prison.”
Her castmates were stunned by Hostin’s revelation, some appearing to disagree with her position in the jury.
Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said, “And you got this guy off?” as Hostin described the grisly crime. Star Jones, who was seated next to Hostin, joked, “Excuse me, can I move over?”
Speaking about the Clancy case, Hostin called Massachusetts’ insanity defense “well-established” and said she agreed Clancy was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity.
Clancy’s defense argued she was not criminally responsible for killing her three children because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

Some jurors have said one holdout juror did not want to acquit. That juror, Michael P. Desronvil, spoke out last week, saying in a statement, “Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she [Clancy] knew exactly what she was doing and planned.”

title: Over 100 people suffered brain injuries on X2 rollercoaster at Six Flags, victims’ lawyers say
summary: Three people say they sustained “catastrophic brain damage” on the California coaster and have sued the amusement park.
story: Three people who say they sustained “catastrophic” brain injuries riding the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California have sued the amusement park and the ride manufacturer for damages, court records show.

And, according to their lawyers, more than 100 other people also sustained brain injuries in the last two years riding what is billed as a roller coaster that “will have even the most hardened thrill seeker screaming.”

“These families, these people, went to Magic Mountain for some entertainment, for some family fun, and they suffered catastrophic brain damage,” attorney Gary Dordick said Tuesday at a news conference.

The lawsuits, filed Monday in California Superior Court, name as defendants Six Flags, several other people and S&S Worldwide, the manufacturer of the roller coaster. The injured riders are seeking unspecified damages.
Six Flags and S&S Worldwide did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The X2 has been closed since July 12, according to NBC Los Angeles.
“The design of this ride makes it inherently dangerous and makes it dangerous in a way that no reasonable rider would expect,” said attorney Christopher Bulone, who works with Dordick.
The X2 is a 200-foot-high roller coaster in Los Angeles County with rotating seats that spin as the ride twists and dives and flips along a track at speeds of up to 76 mph, according to Six Flags.
“Quite simply, you will be spun into another dimension,” the park promises.
Pamela Guillen was celebrating her daughter Camille Marquez’s 16th birthday at the park on July 5 when “she boarded X2 at her daughter’s urging.”
During the ride, Guillen repeatedly hit her head against the ride’s headrest, Dordick said.

“When X2 returned to the station, Camille looked at her mother and saw her sitting with a vacant stare and her mouth open,” the lawsuit says. “Camille initially thought Pamela was joking. She quickly realized that something was wrong.”

“Confused and unstable on her feet,” Guillen landed in the hospital, where surgeons had to remove part of her skull to treat her, and she did not regain consciousness for two weeks, according to the lawsuit.
Six Flags knew Guillen had been hurt but “continued to operate X2 without adequately investigating the cause of her injury or warning subsequent riders,” the lawsuit says.
And six days after Guillen was injured, Naomi Greer-Wilkinson, 25, “lost consciousness” after having ridden the X2 with her siblings on July 11.
Wilkinson underwent “multiple” operations to relieve the pressure on her brain but remains bedridden and barely conscious and is described in the court papers as “an incompetent adult.”

“Naomi had no idea, when she was going to Magic Mountain with her siblings and her friends, that she was signing up for something that could potentially rip the veins in her skull, cause catastrophic bleeding, and lead to a coma,” Bulone said.
The third lawsuit was filed on behalf of lawyer Michael Wilk, who said he was injured after he rode the X2 on Feb. 7.
“Michael’s head began slamming violently against the headrest of his seat,” the lawsuit says. “Immediately upon exiting the ride, Michael felt ill.”

In the weeks that followed, the suit says, Wilk’s co-workers noticed he was struggling and told him to see a doctor. An MRI examination revealed massive brain bleeding and swelling, according to the lawsuit.
Wilk underwent two operations to “relieve the pressure the bleeding was placing on his brain.”
Wilk, according to his lawsuit, can no longer practice law and “continues to suffer debilitating headaches, confusion, dizziness, memory loss and personality changes.”
Word of the lawsuits came in the wake of an investigation by CNN last month that documented at least two deaths and more than a dozen reports of serious injuries and hospitalizations by X2 riders.

title: Mystery men emerge from New York City sewers near Netanyahu’s hotel
summary: The NYPD insists there’s no threat to the prime minister or the United Nations.
story: Security cameras near a New York City hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was planning to stay captured three men emerging from sewers before dawn Wednesday, police said.
The appearance by the mysterious scavengers does not appear to be connected to Netanyahu or the ongoing United Nations General Assembly in Manhattan.

“We have seen a number of incidents over the past few months of individuals going into the sewer system to look for valuables and other scrap metal after a storm,” New York police said in a statement.

“This incident fits that same criteria, but out of an abundance of caution given the U.N. General Assembly and the sensitivity of the location, the NYPD is conducting additional security sweeps with our federal partners,” the police department said.
The three men popped out from the sewer at about 4:30 a.m. and left by car.
The police department has “a robust response to these incidents, which were deployed overnight and additional measures today,” police added.
It’s believed the men were behind similar incidents, mysteriously emerging from city sewers, captured on video this year.
The men, not affiliated with any public works crews, were seen climbing out of manholes in various Brooklyn neighborhoods in late May.

title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years on New York sex crime conviction
summary: The former film producer pleaded not guilty and denies all allegations of nonconsensual sex.
story: Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison Wednesday, more than a year after a jury found the former Hollywood mogul guilty of sexually assaulting former “Project Runway” production assistant Miriam Haley in a high-stakes retrial.
Weinstein appeared in the downtown Manhattan courtroom in a wheelchair, his hands cuffed to his seat.
In a victim impact statement read aloud in the courtroom, Haley said Weinstein “abused his position and power,” causing a “devastating effect on my life and security.”
“It is a life sentence for me,” Haley said.

Weinstein also addressed the court, again denying the allegations against him while apologizing to “anyone I may have hurt by my actions.” He had pleaded not guilty to a charge of first-degree criminal sexual act.
“I am not a perfect person,” he said, “but I am a person who has made mistakes.” He later added: “I am not a violent man.”

Judge Curtis Farber excoriated Weinstein before handing down his sentence. “You took what you wanted by force, and you have never accepted responsibility,” the judge told the former entertainment industry kingmaker.
Farber said Weinstein’s 15-year sentence will be followed by five years of supervised release and a requirement that he register as a sex offender.

Wednesday’s sentencing came after a protracted series of trials, appeals and courtroom proceedings that have kept Weinstein behind bars since his arrest in 2018, one of the key events of the #MeToo movement.

“Today was about the survivors,” Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said in a statement, adding: “I’m moved, as we should all be moved, by their courage and their steadfastness through what has obviously been a challenging process.”
Six-year legal odyssey

Weinstein was originally convicted in 2020 of third-degree rape involving former aspiring actor Jessica Mann and first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley. He was sentenced to 23 years in prison. But his conviction was overturned in 2024 by a New York state appeals court, and a judge ordered a new trial.

Weinstein was again found guilty in June 2025 of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley, who testified that he forcibly performed oral sex on her in his New York City apartment in 2006. The same jury acquitted him of a separate criminal sex act charge involving allegations from former model Kaja Sokola.

The jurors at Weinstein’s second New York trial could not reach a verdict on the charge related to Mann’s allegation, and a third trial on that charge also ended in a hung jury. In late June, prosecutors declined to try the Mann case a fourth time.

Weinstein was separately convicted in Los Angeles in December 2022 of rape and two counts of sexual assault related to a 2013 assault of an Italian actor and model. He was sentenced by a Los Angeles judge to 16 years in prison in February 2023.
He is set to be resentenced in L.A. after an appeals court vacated his original sentence.

The former producer and film distributor vehemently denies all allegations of sexual misconduct, insisting his sexual encounters were consensual. In all, more than 80 women have accused Weinstein of sexual assault or harassment.

Weinstein once lorded over Hollywood. Miramax, his first distribution label, released seminal independent films like “Clerks” and “Pulp Fiction.” He won an Oscar as a producer of “Shakespeare in Love.” In the early 2010s, his second distribution company scored back-to-back best picture wins for “The King’s Speech” and “The Artist.”

But his reign came crashing down in 2017 after The New York Times and The New Yorker published exposés detailing his alleged pattern of sexual harassment and assault. The first wave of accusations against him in 2017 propelled the #MeToo movement, a reckoning with sexual misconduct by powerful people in high-profile professions.

In recent years, Weinstein’s health has visibly declined, and he has faced various medical issues, including diagnoses of bone marrow cancer, kidney disease and diabetes. He has been held at the Bellevue Hospital prison ward, and he will remain there until he is sent to a state prison.

title: Who Won Season 21 of ‘America’s Got Talent’?
summary: The Season 21 winner of “America’s Got Talent” has been revealed. Find out who won the $1 million prize.
story: The Season 21 winner of “America’s Got Talent” has been revealed.

During the season finale on Sept. 23, the latest act to join the roster of champions was announced in an episode that began with 10 acts vying to win this season’s competition, as well as the $1 million prize.
Here’s what happened.
Who Won “America’s Got Talent” 2026?

Nene Royal took home the most votes to win “America’s Got Talent.” After host Terry Crews revealed her name, the 16-year-old rocker from Thailand, who began playing guitar at age 7, collapsed on the stage and covered her eyes in disbelief as the stage was covered in confetti.
“I’m very happy,” she told Crews. “I’m emotional right now. I just want to say thank you to all you guys supporting me and voting.”

Royal emerged as a force to be reckoned with during her audition, when she covered “Zombie” by The Cranberries. She later was invited back to perform in the new Judges’ Callbacks round and advanced right to the live shows after a stellar rendition of “Hysteria” by Muse!

Royal then wowed fans with her take on Soundgarden’s “Black Hole Sun” by Soundgarden in the quarterfinals, which prompted judge Mel B to move her into the finals with the Golden Buzzer. During her finale performance, Royal got a standing ovation from the judges with her performance of The White Stripes’ “Seven Nation Army.” She also performed “The Emptiness Machine” with Linkin Park during the results show.
The judges loved Royal’s finale performance. Howie Mandel said she was “the biggest, most talented, most viral talent to be on that stage,” while Mel B said she was “unique.”
“We can’t get enough of you,” Sofia Vergara added.
Who Came in Second Place?

Magician Geno Ploege was the runner-up. The Wisconsin native has performed around the country and even interned under previous “AGT” champion Mat Franco. The two also performed together during the finale.

The episode began with the top 10 finalists still in the hunt to win this season’s edition of the show. Royal and Ploege were joined by Acro Canine Crew, Come Here, Hundred Fingers, Noelle, Olivia Befus, Royal Lasers, Unitree and Veronika Goroshkova.
Who Made the Top 5?

The 10 acts where whittled down to five. Royal and Ploege advanced, as did Royal Laser, Hundred Fingers and Goroshkova. After that, the competition was narrowed down to a final three: Royal, Ploege and Hundred Fingers, a magic and dance group from South Korea.

title: 61-Year-Old Singer Gets 4-Chair Turn and the Respect of Coaches on Final ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere Night
summary: “The Voice” Season 30 kicked off with three episodes with singers joining either Team Adam Levine, Kelly Clarkson, Queen Latifah or Riley Green.
story: “The Voice” is back, the red chairs are turning and coaches are filling up their teams.
Season 30 of the NBC singing competition show kicked off on Monday, Sept. 21 with a two-hour premiere, followed by a second episode on Sept. 22.
Returning coaches Adam Levine, who won the previous season, and Kelly Clarkson welcomed Queen Latifah and Riley Green to the show as the Blind Auditions began.

During the first episode, host Carson Daly introduced the “First In Button,” which means that whichever coach turns first in a multi-chair turn has the chance to claim an artist before the artist’s final decision. They can only use this button once. Additionally, there are no blocks this season.

Also new is the “TikTok artist of the season.” All season long, the show will be tracking which contestants get the most likes and views on the show’s TikTok. The finalist with the most overall likes and shares will nab the title at the end of Season 30.
Check out “The Voice” Season 30 premiere highlights from the first and second episodes, including which coaches nabbed the first artists.
What Happened During ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?

During the Sept. 21 premiere, Queen Latifah was the first coach to land an artist on her team after a three-chair turn. Riley had a special moment singing his song “My Way” with a contestant, while Kelly offered up her hair extension to an artist so she could join her team.
A country-singing sister duo got the first four-chair turn of the night, and Queen Latifah used her “First In Button” to steal a singer from Kelly and Riley.
The “Worst Way” crooner also used his adorable pup Carl to convince a young star to join his team, but unfortunately it did not work.
The banter between the coaches kept the show feeling fun and flowing, as they poked fun at new coach Riley, his good looks and how he would win over the country singers.
What Happened During Night 2 of ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The Sept. 22 episode kicked off with Queen Latifah arriving on a motorcycle, impressing her fellow coaches.
The first singer of the night, 15-year-old Koumba Diallo, instantly impressed Queen Latifah after just one line. After receiving a four-chair turn, she had one tough decision to make.

Queen Latifah continued pulling out impressive stunts, including bringing backup singers to the stage when convincing an artist to join her team. (It worked!) Kelly also used her “First In” button to nab a soulful singer.
Adam, meanwhile, continued to be conservative with his chair turns, but a contestant singing a country song caught his attention. He, however, had to fight Riley for the aspiring star.

The episode ended with a cliffhanger after another four-chair turn got the coaches hyped. Adam and Kelly were making their best effort to nab  23-year-old Lexi Stephens from New York City, who they said could be the next winner.
Who did she choose? Viewers will find out on Night Three of “The Voice” Season 30 premiere week.
What Happened During Night 3 of ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The third episode began where it left off, with Lexi ultimately choosing Adam as her coach.

It was a special moment when 61-year-old Kyle Davis took a chance on continuing his singing dreams and auditioned for “The Voice.” Strumming along on his guitar, he received a four-chair turn that made him emotional.
There was also a powerhouse singer that Queen Latifah added to her team, while a tween captured the heart of Kelly.

After a stunning rendition of “Moon River” from Amanda Mikkel earned her a four-chair turn, it was her turn to choose a coach. Or was it? Eager to get her on their team, Adam went for it and used his “First In” button.

title: Nathan Fielder Releases Full Trailer for Elizabeth Holmes Doc. What to Know About ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: Director Nathan Fielder has released the full trailer for “You Can See Everything,” a doc about Elizabeth Holmes’ final days a free woman before she entered federal prison.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.

After sharing an unsettling teaser from his upcoming documentary about Theranos founder and convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes, director Nathan Fielder has released the full trailer that shows the businesswoman still maintaining she did nothing wrong.
“You Can See Everything,” also from filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, follows Holmes during her final days as a free woman with partner Billy Evans and their children before she entered prison in 2023.
The trailer reveals that Fielder moved into Holmes’ house for the documentary.
“I think this is the moment in time to capture this story before I’m gone,” she seemingly tells the comedian at one point.
Evans is also featured. Fielder questions him in the clip about the start of his relationship with Holmes, asking Evans if he can truly trust her.
Even Fielder wonders if Holmes is being honest with him during their chats.
“That’s because I don’t have anything to hide,” she tells him as ominous music grows louder.

Just a few hours after Fielder shared the link for the trailer, it racked up over 2 million views on YouTube. Interest in “You Can See Everything,” out in theaters Oct. 16, has continued to grow since it had its worldwide premiere at a secret screening during the Telluride Film Festival.
Critics raved about the movie, which has a 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, and teased its unpredictability.
So, what can you expect from the buzzy documentary?
Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was in attendance when “You Can See Everything” was screened Sept. 6 at the festival.
Read on to find out what she shared about the jaw-dropping reactions from those in the crowd.
What Happened at the ‘You Can See Everything’ Telluride Film Festival Screening?
“You Can See Everything” has gone viral since it was screened at the Telluride Film Festival earlier this month, with attendees having strong reactions.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” Keegan told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.

Holmes was the founder and CEO of the tech startup Theranos, which promised to revolutionize blood testing. She was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab following reports that the technology did not work and could deliver faulty results.
The new documentary features footage of Holmes with partner  Evans and their two children at a rental home in San Diego before Holmes’ sentence began. She is scheduled to be released in 2031.
“I think part of the film is exploring this question of Elizabeth Holmes’s perception of reality and about things that she’s done,” Keegan said.
The teaser trailer released by the studio A24 on Sept. 6 showed a wide-eyed Holmes awkwardly only inches away from Fielder’s face as she spoke to him in one scene.

“I’m not that person,” Holmes said in the clip. “I can promise you that. I don’t have anything to deceive you on. Of course, I’m not deceiving you. I’m engaging with you as a human being. Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that.”
“OK. All right. OK, good chat,” Fielder replies.
The two then stare at each other for an uncomfortable duration.
“You’re being real right now?” Fielder asks.
“I’m always being real,” Holmes replies.
Keegan described the “strange feeling” produced by the interactions between Fielder and Holmes in the film.
“Fielder is very much a character in the film, and in some ways, it’s him trying to understand whether he believes Elizabeth Holmes or not,” Keegan said.

“I’m struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced,” Fielder said during the post-screening Q&A, according to Keegan. “I don’t know why they want me there. I’m a weird guy. I don’t get it. That messed with my head.”

The conversations between Holmes and “The Rehearsal” star are reportedly not the only surreal moments in the documentary. The film also includes an A-list Hollywood actor reenacting Fielder’s conversations with Holmes from prison. Fielder asked the attendees at the screening not to reveal the actor’s identity, according to Keegan.
NBC News reached out to Holmes for comment, but did not hear back. Holmes also shared the movie trailer on her X account on Sept. 6 and wrote, “I’m always being real.”

“You Can See Everything” is the latest screen adaptation of the saga involving Holmes. HBO released the documentary “The Inventor” about Holmes in 2019, and then Amanda Seyfried played her in the 2022 Hulu series “The Dropout.”

title: ‘Home Improvement’ Star Jonathan Taylor Thomas Detained for Obstruction and Public Intoxication
summary: Jonathan Taylor Thomas, best known as Randy Taylor on “Home Improvement,” was arrested for obstruction and public intoxication.
story: Jonathan Taylor Thomas, best known for playing Randy Taylor on “Home Improvement,” was arrested on Sept. 21, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department confirmed.

The sheriff’s department told NBC News that the 45-year-old actor, whose given name is Jonathan Taylor Weiss, was detained after the car he was riding in was pulled over for a DUI investigation in the Westlake Village, California, area.

“Deputies saw a vehicle stopped at the intersection, with a green light blocking traffic. Deputies pulled alongside the vehicle to see if the driver needed assistance. Deputies noticed the driver was acting odd and appeared to be intoxicated,” the sheriff’s department told NBC News. “Deputies conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle for the violation and conducted a driving under the influence investigation.”

Thomas was a passenger in the car, according to authorities, and also appeared intoxicated. According to the sheriff’s department, while the sobriety tests were being performed on the driver, Thomas “continually exited the vehicle and approached the deputies, distracting them from their investigation.”
“Deputies attempted to detain (Thomas) for obstruction and public intoxication, at which point, (Thomas) kicked a deputy in the stomach,” the sheriff’s department said.

The actor was then arrested and taken to the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station where he was booked on the aforementioned felony charges, officials told NBC News. The driver of the vehicle was also arrested and booked for driving under the influence of alcohol.
According to jail records, Thomas was arrested at 1:50 a.m. on Monday, Sept. 21, and was released on Sept. 22 at 12 p.m.
Reps for Thomas did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.
The sheriff’s department said Thomas’ case will be submitted to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration.

Thomas has kept out of the public eye for years, with his last acting credit being a 2015 appearance on Tim Allen’s show “Last Man Standing,” according to IMDb. He also directed a 2016 episode of the series.
Back in July, his former “Home Improvement” on-screen mom Patricia Richardson posted a photo with him and cast member Taran Noah Smith on Instagram.
Thomas, a ‘90s heartthrob, is also known for his roles in “Man of the House,” “Tom and Huck,” “Wild America” and “8 Simple Rules,” among others. He voiced young Simba in “The Lion King,” as well.

title: Who Is Bryan Seaver and What’s Happening With Dolly Parton’s Estate Lawsuit?
summary: Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew who announced her death to the world, is being sued by her estate management company for allegedly waging a “campaign of intimidation.”
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines. Here we uncover what to know about the lawsuit affecting the late Dolly Parton’s estate.
Many fans got to know Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew, after he was the one to announce the country icon’s death to the world in a heartfelt video shared on her official social media pages.

Weeks after Parton’s death, Seaver has reemerged in headlines for being at the center of a battle with the “Jolene” singer’s estate. On Sept. 22, She’s Alive, LLC, the entity that manages and protects the star’s professional property, business and more, filed a lawsuit and temporary restraining order against Seaver, claiming her nephew has engaged in an “escalating campaign of intimidation” against the entity, court documents say. The order was granted shortly after it was filed.
But who is Bryan Seaver and what does the lawsuit mean?
Who Is Bryan Seaver?

Seaver — the son of Dolly Parton’s sister Cassie Parton, one of her 11 siblings — served as the singer’s head of security for more than two decades. His professional security services stretch back to at least 2009, when he was credited as artist security for the country star on her television special “Dolly: Live in London O2 Arena,” according to his IMDB. He also had a small role in the star’s 1986 made-for-television musical film “A Smoky Mountain Christmas.”
In the video announcing her death, Seaver shared that Parton’s head of security role was previously fulfilled by his father Larry.

Currently, he serves as the CEO of the security firm Squadron Augmented Protection Services, which offers K9 services, event security and more in addition to estate security, according to his LinkedIn page.
Seaver and his services were terminated by She’s Alive on Sept. 16, according to the lawsuit filed by the estate management company, alleging Seaver made “escalating threats” against the entity.
In a statement sent to TMZ, Seaver and his team told the outlet that they were “dismayed” by the termination.

“We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much,” they said in the statement.
Seaver did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment.
What Was Bryan Seaver’s Relationship to Dolly Parton?

When it comes to his personal relationship with his aunt Dolly Parton, Seaver described himself as close with the country star. He said he was hand-picked by Parton to deliver the news of her death and shared Parton’s final wishes in the Aug. 25 video announcement of her passing.

“This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago before I fully absorbed it as a future reality,” Seaver said, before calling the duty an “honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness.”
Seaver also shared in the video that his touring experience started young, first joining Parton on the road as a child in the early 1980s.
“Dolly opened doors not just for me, but for her entire family to reach the potential we didn’t even know was possible,” he said.
What Does the Lawsuit Allege of Bryan Seaver?

The lawsuit brought by She’s Alive, which is spearheaded by Dolly Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell, claims that Seaver increasingly threatened violence and weaponized fear towards “those associated with Ms. Parton’s legacy” in an effort to inflict harm for “personal gain.”
Some of the alleged threats detailed in the lawsuit include one in which he reportedly said he was “going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s Brand partnerships.”

She’s Alive also accused the former head of security of making “repeated, written threats” to the country star’s staff, partners, legal and business advisors and others. And due to Seaver’s previous claims of being a “former security operative with a military-contractor background,” many of those allegedly impacted by the threats are either afraid to come to work or have resigned entirely out of safety concerns, the lawsuit alleges.

“For example, in writing within just the past four weeks, Mr. Seaver has claimed to be ‘a killer,’ ‘an international arms dealer’ and a ‘mercenary,’” the lawsuit says. “He wrote, ‘All I do is warfare. Everyone needs to be worried about what I might do.’”
In another alleged instance mentioned in the lawsuit, Seaver wrote about his reported business dealings with Haiti on the day of Parton’s passing.
“I’m a killer,” Seaver wrote, according to the lawsuit. “I sold 27 million $ worth of ammunition and arms to the Haitian Police on the day Dolly died.”
The sequence of events, the lawsuit says, led She’s Alive to terminate Seaver’s services.

Through the lawsuit, the entity is seeking to block Seaver and his associates “permanently” from engaging in threatening behavior and intimidation tactics, ultimately prohibiting him from having any contact with the company or individuals involved in business with the estate.
The motion for a temporary restraining order against Seaver was filed and granted the same day.
What Has Bryan Seaver Said About The Allegations?

Seaver did not respond to NBC News’ request for comment on the allegations. In a text reported by the New York Times, Seaver said that his words were being misrepresented. He also said that he is carrying out his own investigation.

“This is a contrived out-of-context explanation of how this went down and it is being done in an effort to solidify me as some sort of opposition to her brand in her legacy,” Seaver told the outlet, “and that is not the case.”
The term “killer,” Seaver said, was one of endearment that Parton would use to describe him, he told the NYT.
“It was a joke we used around her camp,” he told the outlet. “I was her ‘baby boy ninja.’”

Seaver also said in message to the NYT that Nozell had been a longtime friend of his, and that some of the messages he had sent were about the pair’s efforts to keep others from exploiting Parton and her fortune.
“I trusted Danny,” Seaver told the outlet. “And that’s what those messages were, two friends and brothers commiserating on the people that have screwed Dolly over for many many years.”
Nozell did not immediately return NBC News’ request for comment.
Have Other Parton Family Members Spoken Out?
Most of the country icon’s family members have yet to comment on the issue.

Freida Parton, one of Dolly Parton’s younger sisters and aunt to Bryan Seaver, briefly sounded off on the controversy in a social media post Sept. 23. She wrote that there is “no feud within our family.”
“No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate,” Freida Parton wrote. “We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other.”

title: Olivia Jade’s New Campaign References College Admissions Scandal — And Some Have Thoughts
summary: Social media users are split about Olivia Jade Giannulli’s Reformation collaboration, which pokes fun at the college admissions scheme involving her family.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Olivia Jade Giannulli’s latest fashion collaboration is poking fun at her college admissions scandal, but some fans aren’t laughing.

On Sept. 16, fashion brand Reformation launched a new campaign with Giannulli, who goes by Olivia Jade online, with taglines and designs that reference the YouTuber’s past controversy. An email announcing the 26-year-old’s partnership with the brand showed her posing in a sweatshirt that read “College.”
“Since Olivia Jade is a Good Sport, we brought her back to campus for a lesson in getting dressed,” the brand said.

In 2019, Giannulli’s parents, Lori Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli, were two of the most high-profile names linked to a college admissions scheme. Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli were charged with paying fixers to get Olivia Jade Giannulli and sister Bella Giannulli into elite universities. The “Full House” star pleaded guilty to a federal charge of conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud. She served two months in federal prison, paid a $150,000 fine and completed 100 hours of community service. Mossimo Giannulli, who also pleaded guilty, was sentenced to five months, 250 hours of community service and ordered to pay a $250,000 fine.

Read on to learn more about Olivia Jade Giannulli’s Reformation collaboration, including why some fans have said the photos are in poor taste and why others are calling it a “brilliant” marketing strategy.
Why Is Olivia Jade’s Reformation Ad Controversial?
Olivia Jade Giannulli stars in Reformation’s latest campaign that connects to her college admissions scandal.
For the photoshoot, the social media influencer posed in a “College” sweatshirt and snapped pictures on top of school desks in a classroom.
“@oliviajade is back on campus in a crew that suits her better than the other kind,” Reformation captioned the Instagram post announcing the collaboration.

The brand also shared that “100% of net proceeds” from the College Crew Olivia Jade Giannulli is sporting in some of the pictures will be donated to a nonprofit called Yes Scholars. The organization “identifies high-potential students from low-income communities in Los Angeles, New York City, and rural Appalachian North Carolina, and provides them with the long-term support, resources, and educational access required for success through high school, college, and career,” according to its website.
The crew appears to be another nod to the college controversy involving Olivia Jade Giannulli’s family.

Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli previously admitted that they paid $500,000 to Rick Singer and Key Worldwide Foundation to help Olivia Jade Giannulli and Bella Giannulli get accepted into the University of Southern California by having them pretend to be rowing recruits. Federal investigators also said that the couple had their daughters pose for photos on rowing machines that were used in their admissions application.
Reps for Olivia Jade Giannulli did not immediately return TODAY.com’s request for comment.
What Are the Responses to the Campaign?
Social media users reacted to the campaign in the comments beneath the Instagram post. The response was divided, with some questioning the tone of the ad.
“Genuinely asking how are people saying this is genius and clever? This is such a slap in the face and obnoxious in my opinion,” one person said.
“So it’s like funny to commit a crime?” one Instagram user asked.

Another pointed out, “Yikes, what an interesting concept to have a well resourced woman do this campaign and have the proceeds go to under-resourced communities from normal people shopping.. what a let down.”
One person suggested, “The new tag line should be: ‘Environmentally conscious yet socially out of touch.’
But others applauded the collaboration.
“Whoever’s idea this was needs a raise,” one comment read.
Another agreed, writing, “Please give a raise to the marketing team@thank you.”
The comments on Olivia Jade Giannulli’s post about the ad were more positive.
“Making lemonade with lemons,” one person praised.
One fan who approved said, “This is how you turn it around hahaha.”
A third wrote, “This is actually brilliant.”
On TikTok, the conversation continued. Who What Wear journalist Erin Fitzpatrick uploaded a video explaining the ad and included her take.

“I went to USC on my own merit, didn’t have to bribe my way in and I’m still paying my student loans well over a decade after I graduated. I definitely don’t appreciate rich people being handed something that I had to work for,” she began.

She continued, “That said, her parents were convicted, they served prison time, and that is a lot more than you can say for a whole lot of rich people who have done a whole lot of other horrible things and have never seen the inside of a prison cell and never will.”
Another TikTok user called out the campaign for being “extremely out of touch.”
“I don’t know why Reformation approved that, but it’s not funny,” he said.
He added that he didn’t see the humor in giving Olivia Jade Giannulli a platform when her parents committed a crime.

“I don’t know why Reformation thought that that was a joke, especially in this world now where we’re constantly seeing privilege and access being used as a tool to escape consequences,” he further explained.
However, he clarified that his video was not about Olivia Jade Giannulli having to face any consequences for her parents’ actions. His issue was that she was “benefiting” from the scheme.
What Has Reformation Said?
TODAY.com reached out to Reformation for a comment. The brand could not not provide commentary on the situation.
But, Reformation shared more details about the ad.
“People have been studying Olivia’s outfits for a while, so we figured it was time she gave everyone a lesson in dressing for sport,” the brand said.
Adeniz Villar, cultural strategist and talent and brand partnerships executive, tells TODAY.com that Reformation has always had a playful, self-aware approach to marketing.

“Olivia is clearly in on the joke, which is what makes the casting interesting (because) she’s willing to acknowledge a controversial part of her history and poke fun at herself,” Villar says. “And oftentimes for talent, humor can be a way to re-enter the conversation on their own terms.”

While she says that Reformation “understands its own voice” and has a history of using humor and cultural references in their marketing, Villar questions the charitable component. This is where she says the campaign gets “complicated.”
