title: Princess Diana Expressed Doubts About Her Wedding. This Family Member Stopped Her From Calling It Off
summary: Princess Diana expressed doubts over her wedding but was stopped by this close family member, her brother Charles Spencer writes in his memoir.
story: Before her famous royal wedding to the now King Charles III, Princess Diana expressed serious doubts about going through with the marriage, according to her brother.

In his new memoir “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, recalls learning that the princess had gone to their father, John Spencer, expressing that “she could not go through with marriage to a man who clearly did not love her.”
Diana and Charles were first linked in July 1980 and became engaged in February 1981.

Spencer details that Diana had attended the birthday party of Prince Andrew with her fiancé, whom she was very excited to be reunited with, as he had just returned that day from an official trip to New York. Andrew has since been stripped of his royal titles.

Spencer goes on to write, “Diana had dreamt of spending the party at Windsor Castle at her fiancé’s side. But he had shown next to no interest in her, and she — deeply hurt, confused and increasingly concerned — danced with others, including me, instead.”
Diana went to her father to share her feelings of uncertainty after that night. However, Charles Spencer says he didn’t find out the details of the conversation until much later.

Diana’s father, John Spencer, did not support her idea of ending the engagement. “My father was appalled and said it was impossible to pull out of such an enormous commitment at that point,” Spencer writes.
Spencer reflects on why he believes their father responded that way, pointing to his long connection to the royal family and sense of duty to the monarchy.
“He always adored Diana, but what she was proposing was counter to the code on which he had been brought up, and which he never seemed to question.”
Ending the engagement, Spencer says, would have meant “deeply embarrassing the Royal Family.”

Diana ultimately went through with the wedding, marrying Charles on July 29, 1981, at St. Paul’s Cathedral in London. Diana called the wedding “the worst day of my life,” in a series of recordings taped in 1991 for a biography titled, “Diana: Her True Story.”
Their marriage would eventually crumble, the royal pair separating in 1992 and finalizing their divorce in 1996, just a year before her death at 36.
Spencer’s account also notes a happier relationship that formed the night of Andrew’s birthday, when Elton John performed.
“The day after Prince Andrew’s party, with her usual impeccable manners, Diana wrote by hand to Elton John, her letter applauding him for his brilliance the previous night” he says.

Spencer says the exchange marked the beginning of a friendship that would continue throughout Diana’s life and ultimately became one of the most memorable moments at Diana’s funeral in 1997, when John performed a reworked version of “Candle in the Wind.”

title: Simone Biles Says Her Porsche Was Stolen After 3 Masked Intruders Broke Into Her Home: ‘Absolute Insanity’
summary: Simone Biles said three masked intruders stole her Porsche during a frightening break-in at a home she shared in Chicago with husband Jonathan Owens.
story: Simone Biles said three masked intruders stole her Porsche during a frightening break-in at a home she shared in Chicago with husband Jonathan Owens.
The legendary gymnast described what happened in a TikTok video on Sept. 21 in which she wrote in the caption that the luxury car has since been recovered.
Biles, 29, said in the video that she was getting ready to pick up her new car.

“Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,” she said. “Stole the GTS. But that’s another story. If you guys want to know, I’ll do a story time on that.”
Owens, 31, who is a safety for the Indianapolis Colts, previously played in Chicago for the Bears in 2024 and 2025. It’s not clear when the alleged burglary occurred.
“I feel like I need a reality TV show,” Biles said. “The things that happen to me are absolute insanity, and so it would be really easy for producers to just film regularly.”

Several high-profile athletes have been the victims of theft in recent years. A Seattle man was charged in 2025 for allegedly burglarizing the homes of multiple Seattle Mariners players as well as former Seattle Seahawks star Richard Sherman and Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell.
In 2024, the homes of Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce and Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow were burglarized.
Biles added that she and Owens have brought in additional protection after the car theft.
“That is one of the reasons why we also got our Doberman,” she said.

The revelation by the seven-time Olympic gold medalist came three months after she had a health scare she called “one of, if not the scariest experience of my life.” Biles shared the unspecified medical issue on her Instagram story on June 6.

“I’m not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today’s age,” Biles captioned a photo of her wrist with hospital bands on it. “But almost dying wasn’t on my bingo card earlier this week.”
Owens was in training camp with the Colts at the time.
“This was one of, if not the scariest experience of my life. Especially since Jonathan was in Indy for practices,” she wrote.
She then shared on her Instagram story on July 23 that she had a “procedure” that required a hospital visit.
Biles did specify what the procedure concerned or if it was connected to her health scare in June.

title: Taylor Swift Teases First New Song After Wedding: What We Know About ‘Patient Zero’
summary: Taylor Swift says she’s been “impatiently waiting” to share this new song with fans. The singer’s new song, “Patient Zero,” will be released on Sept. 25.
story: It’s a good day to be a Swiftie!
On Sept. 22, Taylor Swift announced that she is releasing a new song titled “Patient Zero” at the end of the week.
“I’ve been impatiently waiting to tell you that my brand new single ‘Patient Zero’ will be out on September 25 (!!!!!!!!!!!!)” the pop star wrote on her Instagram, alongside a new photo of herself.
The single is currently available to pre-order on Swift’s website for 24 hours.
The news comes after Swift has been leaving Easter eggs for fans the past two weeks, making Swifties question if the Grammy winner planned to announce new music.

Swifties first speculated that Swift was up to something when she appeared in a skit at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14. During the sketch, which featured cast members from “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” Swift looked directly into the camera and said, “Saccharide. Aries. From the Vineyard. North or South.”

Swifties immediately started to dissect the meaning, wondering if it pointed toward Swift releasing “Taylor’s Versions” of her debut and “Reputation” albums. For the past week, they have been sharing theories on social media.
One X user posted a tweet that unscrambled the phrase to seemingly reveal a hidden message: “My first record’s re-record is out Nov. 10.”
Then, fans noticed that a letter posted on Swift’s website in May 2025 confirming she purchased her master recordings suddenly  had three pages instead of two.
But theories linking the clues to her debut or “Reputation” albums started to lead to dead ends when zeroes began to appear in her song lyrics on Apple Music and Spotify.
The final piece of the puzzle? Swift updated her Instagram bio to read, “And, baby, that’s sh0w business f0r y0u” the same day a countdown appeared on her website.
All signs lead to “Patient Zero,” which will be Swift’s second release this year. In June, she announced the single “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the “Toy Story 5” soundtrack.
Swift did not confirm if “Patient Zero” will be the lead single from her highly-anticipated 13th album.
Last year, she released “The Life of a Showgirl,” which included hits like “The Fate of Ophelia,” “Opalite” and “Elizabeth Taylor.”
Her 12th album broke a record with its first week sales, selling over 4 million units.

title: Who Was Nance O’Neil and Did She Really Have a Relationship with Lizzie Borden?
summary: Who was Nance O’Neil and did she really have a relationship with Lizzie Borden?
story: An unlikely friendship between a reclusive Lizzie Borden and an international actor is explored in the latest edition of the Netflix series “Monster.”

Borden, who was famously acquitted of murder charges in the hatchet deaths of her father and stepmother in 1893, was living in relative seclusion in 1904 when she met Nance O’Neil, a theater and silent film actor who had performed all over the world.
In “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” O’Neil (Jessica Barden) appears in four episodes, including one about Borden’s life after her acquittal.
Here’s what to know about their friendship and how it’s portrayed in the Netflix series.
Who Was Nance O’Neil?
O’Neil was born Getrude Lamson in 1874 in California, according to her 1965 obituary in The New York Times.
Beginning her acting career at 19, she took the stage name Nance O’Neil in homage to English comedienne Nance Oldfield and tragedienne Eliza O’Neil.

O’Neil was hailed for her theater performances as tragic heroines and performed on “hundreds of stages around the world,” according to her obituary. She performed in the United States, New Zealand, Europe and Australia, drawing notice for her performances in Broadway plays like “The Passion Flower” and “The Lily,” according to Deadline.
She later transitioned to silent films, where she appeared in dozens of movies between 1913 and 1932, per Deadline.
How Did Nance O’Neil and Lizzie Borden Become Friends?
O’Neil was starring in a play in Boston in 1904 when she met Borden, who lived in nearby Fall River, Massachusetts.

After watching her perform, Borden sent O’Neil a bouquet of flowers expressing her admiration for O’Neil’s performance, the actor recalled an article by the New Bedford Standard following Borden’s death in 1927.
Their friendship “purportedly scandalized (Borden’s) more retiring sister,” Emma Borden, author Cara Robertson wrote in her book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden.”

Following her acquittal in the deaths of her parents in 1893, Borden had remained in her native Fall River but became a pariah. She “lived virtually alone” with “few if any close friends,” according to her 1927 obituary in The New York Times, making O’Neil one of the few who got to know her.
Following her notoriety from the trial, Borden tried to recast herself as “Lizbeth” instead of Lizzie, which Miller writes “may have been O’Neil’s influence.”

O’Neil was one of her few friends, but the relationship only lasted for a couple years. A 1905 story in the San Francisco Call reported O’Neil and her acting company giving a performance at Borden’s Massachusetts mansion named Maplecroft, where she lived with her sister, Emma Borden.

The story reports that O’Neil was an “intimate friend” of Borden’s who had met her a summer earlier at a resort near Boston. Their friendship lasted until O’Neil finished her theater season in the Northeast before she went on a national tour, according to the New Bedford Standard.

There were rumors of a romantic relationship between the two, but no definitive proof in any letters or writings by either woman. Their relationship was also dramatized in the 2010 theater production “Nance O’Neil.”
Borden never married, while O’Neil married British actor Arthur Hickman in 1916 and remained with him until his death in 1931.
O’Neil told the New Bedford Standard that Borden seemed “utterly lonely,” while noting that Borden’s notoriety for the murder trial did not matter to her.

“It did not alter our relations in the least,” she said. “Of course, the tragedy itself was never mentioned between us; never was there ever so much as an  allusion to it. I simply felt a great sympathy for her, and a great deal of admiration for the way she carried on.  She was always so alone.”

Borden, who secured a large inheritance following the death of her father and stepmother, may have helped out O’Neil financially. She helped her get out of debt to creditors and her manager, according to The Lizzie Borden House.
The two did not keep in touch after O’Neil resumed acting around the country and internationally.
“We were like ships that pass in the night and speak to each other in passing,” she told the New Bedford Standard.
How Is Their Friendship Portrayed in ‘Monster’?
Aspects of their friendship, real and imagined, appear in “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.”
Borden, played by Ella Beatty, is first shown seeing O’Neil onstage at a play in Boston.
“She’s enchanting,” Borden says.
After Borden greets O’Neil following the play, she asks her to dinner at her home.
O’Neil pops up in another episode in which she is shown imparting dramatic techniques to help Borden prepare for being on trial in the deaths of her father and stepmother.
It’s impossible for that sequence to have happened because the two didn’t meet until 1904, 12 years after the murders and 11 years after Borden’s acquittal.
In the final episode of the show, which details Borden’s life following her acquittal, Borden shows O’Neil the manicured landscaping and her menagerie of animals around her opulent Maplecroft estate.
O’Neil regales guests at dinner with her tales of performing in Europe, Egypt, Hawaii and Australia. The rumored financial relationship between Borden and O’Neil is also dramatized in the episode.
“Lizzie, it was your patronage that enabled all of it,” O’Neil tells her on the show. “Traveling first class, accommodation worth of a star, and I owe it all to you.”
O’Neil then talks about how she wants to leave the stage to do silent movies in the burgeoning motion picture industry. She also tries to hit up Borden for more money.
A rumored rift between Borden and her sister, Emma, over Borden’s friendship with O’Neil is also hinted at during a dramatic scene at dinner.
Emma Borden, played by Billie Lourd, castigates her sister in front of her dinner guests while calling O’Neil a “pig-s--- actress.”
Emma Borden never spoke about the reason for her rift with her sister in their later years that caused Emma to move out in 1905, so there’s no record that it was caused by O’Neil.

“The happenings in the French Street house that caused me to leave I must refuse to talk about. I did not go until conditions became absolutely unbearable,” Emma Borden said, according to Lizzie Borden’s obituary.

title: ‘The West Wing’ Turns 27: See Rob Lowe Explain the NBC Drama’s Success in 2000 TODAY Interview
summary: In 2000, Rob Lowe spoke with TODAY about what it was like working on “The West Wing” and why the show took steps to be as realistic as possible.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Rob Lowe talking about “The West Wing” on Feb. 18, 2000, during its first season.
“The West Wing” shot out of a cannon when it premiered on Sept. 22, 1999. The NBC drama, about Martin Sheen’s fictional President Jed Bartlet and his staff, was a ratings hit and critical success.

Rob Lowe portrayed Sam Seaborn, the White House deputy communications director, a role he played from the premiere until the fourth season, before returning for an appearance in the show’s seventh and final season. Lowe visited TODAY on Feb. 18, 2000 to chat with Katie Couric about the heavily-hyped series, which would net him an Emmy nomination in 2001.
“The West Wing” won best drama series at the Emmys in 2000, the first of four consecutive years it would collect the award.
“It’s got the buzz,” Couric said about the series.
“I’m so excited. We worked so hard to do it, and to have people just embrace it in the way that they have is, it’s gratifying, and it keeps us really pumped up,” Lowe said.
What Did Then-President Bill Clinton Think About ‘The West Wing’?
Lowe said President Bill Clinton, who was in office when the show premiered, was all for it.
“I had the honor of going to the White House for the first time, and I met the president, President Clinton, and he said, ‘Tell President Sheen, I approve,’” Lowe said in a Clinton voice.
Lowe said Clinton’s staff watched the show, adding that White House personnel told him they felt “The West Wing” did an accurate job depicting life at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.
“I think it’s pretty realistic. I really do, and that’s what they told us when we went and saw our counterparts there,” he said.
Were ‘The West Wing’ Characters Based on Real People?
Couric pointed out that Seaborn seemed like George Stephanopoulos, who was White House communication director in the Clinton White House. Lowe said that’s not true.
“We were pretty clear at the outset to try to not base our characters on anyone, so that the public would hopefully embrace us as new characters in their lives,” he said.
“We’re our own universe that exists unto ourselves,” he added.
Why Did ‘The West Wing’ Deal With Real Issues?

Right from the jump, the show didn’t shy away from addressing tough subject matter. Lowe said it was incumbent on the series to be “very political” and take a “stand,” while also letting the other side of the issues get to speak out.
“We are depicting a liberal democratic presidency, but I have to tell you that if it were a conservative Republican presidency, I think the show would still work as well,” he said.

“You just need to take a position, so people believe that you’re a real White House,” Lowe said, “because at the end of the day, it isn’t so much about what position we take as the humanity and the people that are taking the positions.”

title: All About Princess Diana’s Siblings, Including Charles Spencer
summary: Who are Princess Diana’s siblings? All about Charles Spencer and her sisters, Jane and Sarah, and late brother John.
story: To the world, she was Princess Diana. To her three siblings, she was Diana.
Charles Spencer, Diana’s younger brother, has written a book about his memories of his late sister and her legacy, entitled “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister.”
In an interview with the BBC ahead of “Swan Song’s” release on Sept. 22, Charles Spencer described the sister he knew: “She was just phenomenally good fun,” he said.
“We grew up together. I mean, it was never a dull moment,” he said.

Diana’s parents, John Spencer, the 8th Earl Spencer, and Frances Shand Kydd, were married for 15 years, and had five children over the course of their marriage. Their son, John, born before Diana, died in infancy. Diana also had two older sisters, Lady Sarah McCorquodale and Lady Jane Fellowes.

Charles Spencer, who is also a historian, told the BBC he is writing the book out of “duty” as an “eyewitness to history.” His sister was a beloved global figure at the center of one of recent history’s most scrutinized marriages.
Diana married the now King Charles III in 1981, and their tumultuous marriage led to separation in 1992 and divorce in 1996. She died a year later in 1997, a mother of two and just 36 years old.
Here’s what to know.
Lady Sarah McCorquodale
Sarah McCorquodale, born in 1955, is the oldest of the Spencer siblings. She was also the reason her younger sister met the then Prince Charles in the first place.

Sarah met Charles at a party in 1977 and the two were romantically linked for about a year. During that time, Charles encountered Diana for the first time. Sarah made public comments to journalists about their breakup in a 1978 interview.
“There is no chance of my marrying him,” she told TIME. “I’m not in love with him. And I wouldn’t marry anyone I didn’t love whether he were the dustman or the King of England.”
In “Swan Song,” Charles said Diana and Sarah shared a “similar energy and innate naughtiness.”
Lady Sarah and her husband Neil Edmund McCorquodale have three children: Emily, George and Celia McCorquodale.
Lady Jane Fellowes
Lady Jane Fellowes, born Cynthia Jane Spencer, was born in 1957.

Jane has lived a relatively private life. She has had few public media appearances or interviews aside from royal funerals, including that of Princess Diana, where Jane read a poem in her sister’s honor, according to BBC.
In 1978, she married Lord Robert Fellowes, a secretary to Queen Elizabeth. Jane and Robert welcomed three children: Laura, Alexander and Eleanor Fellowes. Robert Fellowes died in 2024.
John Spencer
John Spencer was born in January 1960 and died soon after. Charles Spencer posted a photo of his grave in 2022.
Diana was born 18 months after John.
Charles Spencer
Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer, is the younger brother of Princess Diana.
Charles’ new book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” out Sept. 22, has catapulted him into the zeitgeist, as the book contains strong commentary about King Charles and the royal family.
Born in 1964, three years after Diana, Charles wrote about their relationship in “Swan Song.”

“We were both quite reserved with strangers, and extremely outgoing with friends. We shared a natural stubbornness when pushed — particularly when we felt such pressure was unjust. We tended to look out for one another, often pretty fiercely. Strong early bonds were formed,” he wrote.
He said that she grew up with a “clear objective in mind: to marry for love.”
“She was sure that this was the most important thing, so she could avoid the divorce that had overtaken our parents and devote herself to the children she was always so keen to have,” he wrote.
Charles was 17 when his sister became engaged to Prince Charles. He said he thought hat she would “be fine” in her new role, but never expected her to become a “global sensation.”

“The great unknown back then was the unique spirit within Diana. Hers was an extraordinarily original force that exploded onto the world stage, charged by charisma, embellished by good looks, and underpinned by a completely natural way of connecting people,” Charles wrote.
Beyond “Swan Song,” he is a historian, broadcaster, journalist and author of multiple works of nonfiction including “Blenheim: Battle for Europe” and “Killers of the King.”
After his father, John Spencer, died in 1992, he inherited the Spencer earldom.
Charles has seven children from three marriages. He married Professor Cat Jarman, his fourth wife, in 2026.

title: What Princess Diana Said About King Charles, from Their Marriage to Their Children
summary: Read what Princess Diana had to say about her marriage to Prince Charles, who became King Charles.
story: To the outside world, Princess Diana and then-Prince Charles seemed to have a fairytale relationship. But over time, royal watchers discovered that there was a great deal of turmoil in the couple’s marriage.

The future king first met his bride-to-be in 1977. At the time, Diana was 16 years old and Charles was nearly 13 years her senior. In 1980, the duo began dating then got engaged in February 1981. Five months later, they said “I do” in a televised wedding ceremony.
The royal couple soon started a family and welcomed their first child, a son named William, in 1982, followed by a second son named Harry in 1984.

The couple’s seemingly picturesque life was filled with turmoil behind the scenes and they went on to separate in 1992. By 1995, Queen Elizabeth II recommended that they end their marriage for good, and the divorce was finalized in August 1996.

Before her death in a car accident in 1997, Diana spoke candidly about her relationship with Charles on several occasions, most notably in a series of recordings for a biography titled, “Diana: Her True Story.”
Now, the princess’s brother, Charles Spencer, is giving an intimate look at his sister’s life in his new memoir, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister.”
Before the book is released on Sept. 22, we’re taking a look back at what Diana said about her marriage to Charles and her life as a mother of two princes.
On the wedding:

Charles and Diana became husband and wife on July 29, 1981. The couple exchanged vows at St. Paul’s Cathedral in London in a televised wedding ceremony. Per the BBC, the broadcast was viewed by 750 million in 74 countries.
A 2017 National Geographic documentary titled “Diana: In Her Own Words” used audio from a series of interviews Diana participated in for her biography, “Diana: Her True Story.”
In the documentary, Diana described the feeling of bliss she experienced on her wedding day.

“I remember being so in love with my husband that I couldn’t take my eyes off him. I just absolutely thought I was the luckiest girl in the world and you know, he was going to look after me,” she said.
However, the day was largely overshadowed by feelings of sadness. Diana said she “cried a lot” after her wedding rehearsal earlier in the week because “the tension suddenly hit me.”
Diana went on to describe her wedding as “the worst day of my life.”
“I don’t think I was happy,” she recalled in a recording.
“I never tried to call it off in the sense of really doing that, but I think (it was) the worst day of my life,” she continued.
As she was walking down the aisle, Diana said she spotted Camilla Parker Bowles, one of Charles’ former flames.

According to Penny Junor’s biography of Camilla, “The Duchess: The Untold Story,” the future king was heartbroken when she married another man in 1973. Flash forward to 1978, and the former couple were still close friends. Junor’s book claims that Charles and Camilla even rekindled their romance briefly in “1978 or early 1979.”
While recalling the moment she spotted Camilla on her wedding day, Diana said, “And I thought, ‘Well, there we are. That’s it. Let’s hope that’s all over with,’” she said.
Per Jonathan Dimbleby’s authorized biography of Charles, the future king once again rekindled his romance with Camilla in 1986, while both were still married to other people.
In 1995, Camilla and her husband got divorced. Charles and Diana made their divorce official the following year. Charles and Camilla later got engaged and married in 2005.
On their honeymoon:
After their wedding, the newlyweds embarked on a cruise around the Mediterranean on a royal yacht then spent time in Scotland.
In 2026, a letter Diana wrote after her wedding went up for auction. Per The Telegraph, the letter was sent to her former classmate Katherine Hanbury.

“We had a blissful honeymoon with endless sun and luckily calm seas… we are now up in Scotland until the end of October, which is a big treat for us — I adore being outside all day & hate London!” the princess wrote.
In the letter, which was written two months after her wedding, Diana wrote that it was “wonderful being married” and described it to “a case of playing with grown ups.”

In 1992, biographer Andrew Morton published a biography titled “Diana: Her True Story.” Per People, the author asked one of Diana’s close friends to interview Diana then used those recordings to write the book.
In the biography, Morton described the pain Diana felt on her honeymoon as she became fixated on her husband’s connection with Camilla Parker Bowles.
“At night, I dreamt of Camilla the whole time,” she said, adding that she was “obsessed by Camilla totally.”
Per People, Diana saw two photos of Camilla fall out of her husband’s diary during their honeymoon. Before their wedding, Diana also found a “goodbye” bracelet the groom was going to give Camilla.
In his biography of Diana, Morton described how Charles and Diana had a fight during their honeymoon when he wore a pair of cufflinks Camilla had given him.

“Cufflinks arrive on his wrists — two ‘C’s entwined like the Chanel ‘C’s. Got it in one; knew exactly. ‘Camilla gave you those, didn’t she?’” Diana said. “He said, ‘Yes, so what’s wrong? They’re a present from a friend.’ And, boy, did we have a row.”
In the documentary “Diana: In Her Own Words,” Diana recalled how her husband brought eight books with him on vacation.
“We were never on our own,” she said.
The princess also discussed her struggles with disordered eating, which was ever-present during her honeymoon.
“By then the bulimia was appalling,” she said. “It was four times a day on the yacht.”
On their kids:
During their marriage, Diana and Charles welcomed two sons named William and Harry.
In 1995, Diana sat down with BBC Panorama for a controversial interview with journalist Martin Bashir. During their chat, she said that she always wanted to be a mother.

“I came from a family where there were four of us, so we had enormous fun there,” she said. “And then William and Harry arrived — fortunately two boys, it would have been a little tricky if it had been two girls — but that in itself brings the responsibilities of bringing them up, William’s future being as it is, and Harry like a form of a back-up in that aspect.”
Diana discussed her “difficult pregnancy” and said she also experienced “post-natal depression” after delivering William.

“I received a great deal of treatment, but I knew in myself that actually what I needed was space and time to adapt to all the different roles that had come my way. I knew I could do it, but I needed people to be patient and give me the space to do it,” she said.
In the documentary “Diana: In Her Own Words,” Diana described the period between welcoming William and Harry as “total darkness” as the troubles in her marriage intensified.
“I can’t remember much. I’ve blotted it out. It was such pain,” she said.
However, the princess recalled how she and Charles were “very, very close” to each other during the six weeks before Harry was born, saying they were “the closest we’ve ever been.”
“And then as suddenly as Harry was born, it just went bang, our marriage. The whole thing went down the drain,” she said.
Diana added that Charles wanted a daughter, so she didn’t tell her husband when she found out that she was expecting another son.
“He wanted two children and he wanted a girl,” she said.

During her interview with Bashir, Diana said her biggest hope for her sons was that they develop “an understanding of people’s emotions, people’s insecurities, people’s distress, and people’s hopes and dreams.”
Diana described William as a “deep thinker” in the interview and described Harry as “complete joy” in the documentary “Diana: In Her Own Words.”
On their divorce:

Diana and Charles separated in 1992 and ultimately divorced in 1996. According to Diana, factors that led to the divorce included “pressure of the media” and adultery. Charles admitted to being unfaithful in a 1994 interview. She also described depression and developed an eating disorder during her marriage, she told Bashir.
Speaking to Bashir, Diana said her own parents’ divorce made her want to “make it work” even more.
“I desperately wanted it to work, I desperately loved my husband and I wanted to share everything together, and I thought that we were a very good team,” she said.
When Diana learned that news of Charles’ infidelity was going public, she was concerned about how it would affect her sons.

“William asked me what had been going on, and could I answer his questions, which I did. He said, was that the reason why our marriage had broken up? And I said, well, there were three of us in this marriage, and the pressure of the media was another factor, so the two together were very difficult. But although I still loved Papa I couldn’t live under the same roof as him, and likewise with him,” she continued.
Diana told Bashir that she took responsibility for the end of the marriage: “We both made mistakes.” For example, she admitted to infidelity on her own end in the interview.

“I take full responsibility, I take some responsibility that our marriage went the way it did. I’ll take half of it, but I won’t take any more than that, because it takes two to get in this situation,” she said.

title: Presley Gerber Shared Mental Health, Addiction Struggles Before Death: ‘I’ve Had a Lot of Time to Look Into Myself’
summary: Presley Gerber shared his struggle with mental health and addiction before his death in a rehab facility at 27. What he said about drugs, alcohol, depression.
story: Presley Gerber was open about his struggles with mental health and substance use before his death at 27.
The son of model Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber passed away Sunday.
“The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” a statement on behalf of his family noted.
Gerber, who began modeling as a teen, once called dealing with mental health issues a “24/7 job” and posted candid videos he called “Mental Health Mondays” on his Instagram page.
How Did Presley Gerber Die? What We Know
Gerber died at a “rehab facility,” according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
No cause of death was given, but an exam of his body has been scheduled, the website entry notes.
Police responded to a report of a possible overdose at about 9:35 a.m. on Sunday, Sept. 20, and found “an adult male who was deceased,” the Santa Monica Police Department said in a statement.
Detectives are investigating the death “as a suspected overdose. At this time, there is no indication of foul play,” the statement noted.

A law enforcement source told NBC News that he was found unresponsive at the rehab facility in Los Angeles on Sunday morning. He had checked into the facility at 10 p.m. the night before. The sourced added that he had likely been dead for some time when he was found in the room where he was sleeping.
He Spoke About Mental Health at an Event a Few Months Before His Death

In June, Gerber appeared with his parents at an event in Malibu, California, where he took part in a “candid panel discussion about mental health,” People magazine reported. It was his last public appearance.
“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” he told the audience.
The model also offered advice about boosting mental health: “Move your body regardless of how you’re feeling. Get outside. Get some sun,” he said. “If you don’t feel like moving, lay on the grass.”

In December 2025, Presley spoke about his struggles in a since-deleted video on Instagram, revealing he’d largely given up drinking in recent years, noting that alcohol was “no longer serving” him, E! News reported.

He said he was taking various medications including Valium — the brand name for diazepam, which is used to relieve anxiety and control agitation caused by alcohol withdrawal — and buprenorphine, a medication to treat opioid use disorder, according to E! News.

He added he was also taking Xanax, the brand name for alprazolam, which is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders, for “when the panic attacks are really, really bad,” but was seeking more direction about his dosages.

“Every psychiatrist I’ve had — and I’ve had, like, 15 — they’re all like, ‘Here’s 20 medications,’” Gerber said. “‘Take this if you feel like this, take this as needed.’ And I’m like, ‘No, don’t give me that much leeway. I need some direction.’”
He Was a Mental Health Advocate
In a 2023 podcast, he said he struggled with mental health and depression, and wanted to help others dealing with similar issues.
“Whether I help one person or a 100 people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s all I need to do,” Gerber said.
“I’ve had a lot of time to look into myself and learn about myself with therapists.”
Mental health is “such a big part of my life,” he added, calling his focus on it a “24/7 job” and noting “there’s no judgement.”

“I’ve seen a lot of stuff and I’ve learned a lot of things, and what I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made,” he said.
He Tried Ibogaine
In a video he posted on Instagram in March, Gerber was seen in Cancun, Mexico, taking part in what he describes as a “Pre Ibogaine Flood Dose — quiet moment before everything changed.”

“I was absolutely terrified,” he writes in the caption. “Letting go of control didn’t come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why i was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, i started finding my way back to myself.”

Ibogaine, a psychoactive compound found in the root of Tabernanthe iboga, a shrub native to Central Africa, has been studied for its potential in treating opioid and alcohol addiction, and other substance use disorders, according to the University of Virginia Division of Medical Toxicology.
It has hallucinogenic properties, and may prevent cravings and withdrawal.
Sister Kaia Gerber Spoke About His Addiction Struggles in a Recent Interview
After Gerber posted the candid video about his struggles in December, his younger sister, Kaia, praised his honesty and vulnerability.

“My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone.’ There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them,” she told Vogue.
The outlet noted that he had a “decade-long struggle with drug addiction.”

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: ‘DWTS’ Pro Witney Carson’s Sons Help Her With Adorable Gender Reveal
summary: Witney Carson and husband Carson McAllister had their two sons help them with their gender reveal. Find out if she’s having a boy or girl.
story: Witney Carson and husband Carson McAllister just found out the gender of baby No. 3.
In a Sept. 21 Instagram video, the “Dancing With the Stars” pro shared how she found out if her family was adding a little boy or a little girl to their crew.
The video shows the couple on a dock with their backs turned while their two sons — Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3 — picked a pink or blue bouquet of flowers, announcing the baby’s gender.
After reading the card that tells them which bouquet to grab, Kevin grabs the blue one, but Jet then picks up the pink one, confusing his parents for a second.
“It’s a boy,” Carson says, as McAllister adds, “Are we just a house full of brothers?”

“Baby McAllister number 3 is a,” the caption reads, which also includes blue hearts and teary-eyed emoji. “We couldn’t be happier or feel more blessed with all these boys. I love being a boy mom. My greatest honor in life is to raise them.”
The couple were congratulated in the comments section by friends, including Robert Irwin, who was Carson’s “DWTS” Season 34 winning partner.
“SO EXCITED,” Irwin wrote, along with a number of blue heart emoji.

“As a mom of three boys, you’ll always have a full dance card for life. It is the best,” one fan wrote, while another added, “This gets me so teary eye because raising boys to be men is such a privilege and the excitement he had when he saw it was a brother is just unbeatable.”
Carson announced that she was pregnant on Aug. 17, weeks before she was confirmed to be returning for Season 35 of “DWTS.”
In an interview with TODAY.com, the dancer shared that she and her husband knew it was time to expand their family.

“We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that,” she said. “Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”
She was determined to continue working, saying she didn’t feel like she had to put work on hold.

“I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family,” she said.” It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”

Carson competed with partner Guillermo Rodriguez on the first night of the two-night “DWTS” Season 35 premiere. During the Sept. 15 episode, they danced a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight, scoring a 10 out of 30.
Though they had the lowest scores of the night, the pair escaped an elimination and are gearing up for their second dance on the Sept. 22 episode.
Carson told TODAY.com that she was “feeling good” and during rehearsals was listening to her body, making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she said. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

title: When Is ‘The Voice’ On? How to Watch the Season 30 Premiere
summary: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
story: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
Celebrating its milestone 30th season, the NBC singing competition show kicks off with a three-night premiere that starts on Monday, Sept. 21.
During her appearance on TODAY ahead of the premiere, Kelly Clarkson called this season “fun” and exciting, especially with the addition of two new coaches.
Carson Daly returns as host, along with coach Adam Levine who won Season 29. Clarkson is back for her 11th season, while the newcomers are Queen Latifah and Riley Green.

Clarkson told TODAY that Green and Queen Latifah’s addition was “seamless.” She then jokingly added it was “annoying” because she does have to “fight really hard” to get country artists on her team now.

During the premiere episode, viewers will see the Blind Auditions, the first round of the show, where singers will showcase their impressive vocals in hopes of getting the coaches to turn their chairs. Once a coach hits their button and shows interest in a contestant, they try to persuade the artist to be on their team.
Find out the date, time and how to watch Season 30 of “The Voice” below.
What Day Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The new season of “The Voice” premieres on Monday, Sept. 21 on NBC.
The Blind Auditions will continue on Tuesday, Sept. 22 and Wednesday, Sept 23.
What Time Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Air?
The first episode of “The Voice” Season 30 will air at 8 p.m. and end at 10 p.m.
The Sept. 22 and Sept. 23 episode will air from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m.
All episodes will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
What to Know About ‘The Voice’ Season 30

“The Voice” is returning to its live shows format following the Blind Auditions and Cut Week, an elimination round. The six weeks of live shows will include special guest appearances and themed weeks. These episodes will be simulcast on Peacock.

During this season’s Blind Auditions, the show is introducing the all-new “First  In  Button.”  The button, which can only be used once, “gives the coach who turns first on a multi-chair turn the opportunity to claim an artist before the artist’s final decision,” the show’s press release said.

title: Who Was Lizzie Borden’s Sister, Emma?
summary: Who was Lizzie Borden’s sister Emma and what happened to her after the trial? Find out the true story of Emma Borden.
story: Lizzie Borden’s sister Emma Borden doesn’t appear all that much in Netflix’s newly released show “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.” However, when she does, she leaves quite an impression as the more accomplished sibling of the household whose inner turmoil plays out during the infamous trial for the gruesome Aug. 1982 murders of the pair’s father and stepmother.
But what was she really like?

The true story of Emma Borden doesn’t quite match that of the “It Girl” character in the series, which was released Sept. 17. While Emma, played by actor Billie Lourd, is portrayed as a foil to her awkward, spinster sister Lizzie, the real-life eldest daughter wasn’t a popular gal, swimming in suitors and often away from home. Rather, experts and historical accounts show that Emma Borden was attached to her younger sister and lived for years, upholding a promise she once made to look after Lizzie Borden.

“More than a passive bystander, she was the emotional rock, the financial guardian, and ultimately, the keeper of secrets that would remain buried forever,” the Lizzie Borden House wrote of Emma Borden on its website.
What Is Emma Borden Like on ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story?’
In the Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan series, Emma is considered the superior child by her stepmother and father. Most of the time, she’s not home, instead spending her days with suitors.

In one scene during the second episode, Emma reveals that high society man Bard Wainwright is courting her. And in that same episode, he asks for her hand in marriage. Emma responds by collapsing elegantly on the fainting couch before enthusiastically agreeing to tie the knot.

“Emma comes and goes with the wind,” Lizzie, played by Ella Beatty, tells maid Bridget as she watches the private engagement through a crack in the door. “Everything a girl could want just falls into her lap.”

In a private conversation with Lizzie, Emma reveals that she has no such intentions of marrying Bard, but plans to string him along “just like the last two.” The eldest daughter explains to Lizzie that she isn’t interested in being “hog-tied to one man for the rest of your life.”

In another standout moment in the conversation, Emma reveals that she will be inheriting the bulk of their father Andrew Borden’s fortune due to her strong will. Lizzie, on the other hand, will be relegated to just 5% of the wealth because she, instead, is “feebleminded.”

Viewers don’t see much of Emma until much further in the series, when she walks into the crime scene and discovers her father’s gory cadaver on the couch. Emma jumps to conclusions and upon seeing her sister, immediately accuses Lizzie of being behind the murders.

While Lizzie is being detained as a suspect, Emma visits the younger sister and expresses doubt around her innocence. She reveals that on their late mother’s deathbed she had promised to always protect Lizzie, but that the shifting narratives and unusual sequence of events make it all difficult.
But when it comes to her actual testimony, Emma makes a resounding defense of Lizzie and is among the key figures who contribute to the younger Borden’s exoneration.

After the trial, Emma turns to laudanum and alcohol to cope with her depression. Gone are the days that men are interested in marrying her, as the Borden name has turned into “a bit of an albatross,” she says. And near the end of the show, she decides she can no longer tolerate the idea of being under her sister’s roof, leaving Lizzie for good.
“I hope that on your deathbed, you admit what you did,” Emma says in her last words to Lizzie.
What Was The Real-Life Emma Borden Like and Where Was She During The Murders?

The “Monster” version of Emma Borden is a sharp departure from the real-life woman. Emma, it turns out, was a quiet, highly conservative person, according to the Lizzie Borden House. And there were simply no records of her ever having a suitor.

As for her relationship to her stepmother, Emma Borden was said to be more resentful of Abby Borden than Lizzie Borden was. Emma, who was 14 when her father remarried, always called Abby by her first name.
“Perhaps her grief foreclosed a warmer relationship with the woman she viewed as her mother’s replacement,” author Cara Robertson wrote in her book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden.”
Robertson also suggests that Emma may have “felt she served as mother to Lizzie and resented Abby’s intrusion.”

And unlike what the show depicted, Emma was not the main beneficiary of the Andrew Borden fortune. In fact, Andrew had used his resources to buy Abby’s family a home — something that did not sit well with the Borden sisters.

“We know that from that point, both Lizzie and Emma blamed their stepmother for their father’s actions,” Robertson previously told TODAY.com “Even though he tried to equalize matters by deeding over some property to them, they viewed their stepmother as having played this negative role in siphoning away Borden money to (Abby’s) family.”
One aspect of the Netflix series’ portrayal of Emma does ring true, however. Robertson’s book points out that Emma once spoke of the promise she made to her mother.
“When my darling mother was on her deathbed she summoned me, and exacted a promise that I would always watch over ‘Baby Lizzie,’” Emma said, according to Robertson’s book.
On the day of the murders, Emma was visiting friends in another town, Fairhaven, Massachusetts, some miles away from the family’s home in Fall River, the book mentions.
It wasn’t until Emma received a telegram that afternoon that she learned about the double homicide, according to the Lizzie Borden House website.
What Was Emma Borden’s Role in The Murder Trial?

During the famous trial that shocked the nation, Emma Borden stepped up, using her inheritance to retain former Massachusetts Governor George D. Robinson along with other heavy-hitting attorneys to defend her sister.
What’s more, Emma put on an invaluable performance during her testimony. As Robertson writes, Emma was the key defense witness who provided the “most potent character support for her accused sister.”
“Fortunately, Emma was up to the difficult task: ‘There was no swaying of her slender form, no dropping of her straight-cut eye, no quivering of her tight-shut mouth,’” Robertson wrote in her book.
What Happened to Emma Borden After Lizzie Borden Was Acquitted?

Though Emma and Lizzie lived in peace for a stretch of time after the murders, moving into an estate they called “Maplecroft” in Fall River’s affluent neighborhood of the Hill, the calm didn’t last forever, according to Robertson’s book.

Following the trial, Lizzie attempted to start a new life, rebranding herself as “Lizbeth” and ingratiating herself with the theater crowd. Emma, Robertson wrote, strongly disapproved. The much more conservative, elder sister sought the advice of her pastor, who encouraged her to move on.
In 1905, more than a decade after the murders, Emma left and never spoke to Lizzie again, according to Robertson’s account.
Emma died just nine days after Lizzie. According to the Lizzie Borden House, Emma was unaware her sister ever died.

title: Trump welcomes Xi for a White House summit set to be high on pageantry, low on substance
summary: Both the U.S. and Chinese leaders are seeking to maintain stability in ties between the world’s two biggest economies, with few concrete results expected from their White House meeting.
story: HONG KONG — President Donald Trump’s strong rapport with Xi Jinping is set to be on display in Washington this week as the Chinese leader makes his first U.S. state visit in more than a decade. But below the surface-level pageantry at the White House, little is likely to be resolved as the world’s two biggest economies continue to spar over trade, Taiwan, AI and more.

Since a trade war shook the global economy last year, U.S.-China relations have been at an effective standstill, experts say, buying both sides time to reinforce their strengths and address their vulnerabilities.

Trump, who usually meets with foreign leaders at the White House, was at the tarmac to greet Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, when they arrived at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, outside Washington on Wednesday.

Trump will be greeting Xi in a weaker position than when they last met four months ago, said Allen Carlson, an associate professor of government at Cornell University, as he faces mounting inflation, falling approval ratings, an unpopular war with Iran and a potentially disastrous midterm election result for his Republican Party.

title: Netanyahu takes the U.N. stage facing global isolation and a fight for his political future
summary: As Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case at the United Nations General Assembly, his target audience will likely be Israeli voters.
story: TEL AVIV — Even as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case to the world at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, his target audience will likely be closer to home: Israeli voters ahead of next month’s crucial elections.
Netanyahu arrived in New York Thursday for what appears to be a whirlwind trip that will highlight the growing isolation of the U.S. ally over its assault on the Gaza Strip.

With only a handful of diplomatic meetings on the sidelines of the assembly and President Donald Trump’s focus firmly on his summit with China’s Xi Jinping, the prime minister looks set to return to Israel shortly after his address to be back in time for the major Jewish Sukkot holiday on Friday evening.

“I am leaving tonight for New York in order to defend, from the U.N. podium, Israel and IDF soldiers,” the prime minister said in a video Wednesday night before he left. “You hear the terrible lies that are being spread there.”

Netanyahu is likely to address an almost empty chamber as delegates observe an annual tradition of walking out in protest over the conduct of Israel’s war in the Gaza Strip. But that spectacle will likely play well among the premier’s domestic supporters, for whom he has styled himself as a defiant truth-teller standing up for Israel on the global stage.

While much of the world has condemned Israel for the huge loss of civilian life and continuing humanitarian tragedy in Gaza, Netanyahu’s primary domestic challenge comes from an Israeli right-wing who accuses him of not being tough enough in the country’s multi-front war on Iran and its proxy groups.

“The main reason that brings him to the UN General Assembly this time is the opportunity to talk, using the UN microphone, to his voters in Israel, in his polished English, in a speech that of course will be accompanied by exaggerated descriptions of his great achievements,” wrote Efraim Ganor, a political, a strategic affairs expert, wrote in the right-leaning Israeli newspaper Ma’ariv.
The few hints that Netanyahu has given about the subject of his speech have focused on populist, patriotic causes.

In a video posted to social media on Tuesday, Netanyahu took aim at a popular target: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who had pledged to arrest him for crimes against humanity before later acknowledging that he lacked the jurisdiction to do so.

Appearing to adopt the posture of a professional wrestler and looking straight into the camera, Netanyahu accused the mayor of supporting Hamas — which Mamdani has strenuously denied — and fomenting riots against New York Jews. He added that he would  “tell the truth about you” and “tell the truth about our heroic soldiers.”
Asked about his comments, Mamdani told a news conference Tuesday that the Israeli military had killed an 11-year-old boy in a zone deemed safe in Gaza, “so that is what I have to say to his video.”

Netanyahu’s mention of Israel soldiers appears to be a reference to “NAZA,” a documentary made by two Israeli filmmakers in which 24 anonymous Israelis, described as military and intelligence officials, talk about the cynical process by which the country’s military evaluated the need for civilian deaths during the Gaza war.
A popular target that has riled Israeli leaders ahead of the elections, “NAZA” has earned plaudits abroad but condemnation at home.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Politicians have stumbled over themselves to publicly condemn the documentary in the harshest terms, with some demanding a criminal investigation into the duo and even stripping them of Israeli citizenship.
In another hint on Wednesday night, Netanyahu, who has a history of peppering his general assembly speeches with props, gags and gimmicks, said his speech would include “surprises.”
Last year, he told the audience that his speech was being broadcast into Gaza through massive loudspeakers and streamed to mobile phones so that Israeli hostages trapped in Gaza could hear him speak.

He also wore an oversized QR code on his jacket, encouraging audiences to activate the code to visit a website with a video showing Hamas’s attacks on Israel in October 2023 that killed about 1,200 people and sparked the latest round of fighting. Israel’s subsequent war in Gaza killed more than 75,000 people, according to Palestinian health official

In the years before that, Netanyahu brandished regional maps to make his points. Two years ago, he displayed two maps that showed the “blessing” of Israel’s influence contrasted with the “curse” of Iran’s expanding power.

And in 2012, more than a decade before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in what they said was an attempt to keep the Islamic Republic from getting a nuclear weapon, Netanyahu held up a cartoon image of an Iranian nuclear weapon with a “red line” for its maximum enrichment level.

title: Yemen says it asked Trump for U.S. military support in fight against Houthis
summary: A senior official said Yemen is seeking help as the Iranian-backed rebels tighten their grip on its Red Sea coast, threatening to further disrupt global energy shipments.
story: The government of Yemen is seeking U.S. military support in its fight against the Houthis, a senior Yemeni official said Wednesday, as the Iranian-backed rebels rapidly expand their control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and threaten another critical Middle East waterway for global energy supplies.

Yemen’s president, Rashad al-Alimi, conveyed the request for U.S. assistance to President Donald Trump in a call this week, Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, vice president of the Yemeni Leadership Council, told reporters on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly.

Asked about a report this week by Reuters, which cited one Yemeni and one Western source as saying Trump made no direct pledge of military support during the call, Bawazir said he was unaware that the request had been rejected.
He said that Trump understands the danger of the Houthis and that “we hope and expect more support for the Yemeni government in the face of the Houthi militias.”
The White House did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment overnight.
Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
Bawazir did not say whether U.S. support should extend to direct military strikes.
“We do not ask the American soldiers to actually go into war on our behalf,” he said. “And we don’t really request that they do nothing.”

Yemen does look forward to “mutual coordination on the intel and security fields,” according to Bawazir, who requested that the U.S. enhance the Yemeni government’s own military capacity to take on the threat.
“The aerial campaigns are important,” he said. “But supporting the Yemeni government and forces on the ground is indeed a guarantor to end the danger of those militias.”

Yemen has been embroiled in various states of conflict since 2014, when the Houthis drove the internationally recognized government out of the capital city, Sanaa, and ignited a regional proxy war, with Saudi Arabia supporting the exiled government against the Iranian-backed rebels.

In their latest military campaign, the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline with the aim of cutting off the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which has become a critical waterway for Saudi Arabia to transport oil after Iran effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia, a critical U.S. ally in the Middle East, including in the U.S. war with Iran, has urged the U.S. to take military action against the Houthis, who further escalated their actions over the weekend by launching an attack on the Saudi capital, Riyadh. So far U.S. support has been limited to providing intelligence and targeting data.

Trump, who announced a ceasefire with the Houthis last year after weeks of punishing strikes against the militant group, went so far as to order strikes against the Houthis on Sunday, NBC News has reported, but the order was canceled hours later.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that the U.S. has made commitments to the Saudis and is living up to them, adding that “obviously, the president has many options available to him.”
Trump said this month that the Houthis, which the U.S. designates as a terrorist organization, don’t want to fight the U.S. and “they don’t want us to go after them.”

“They’ve called and they’ve talked to us, and they don’t want us to,” Trump told reporters while he was in Ireland. “They would much prefer not having us involved, and they’re letting most ships go through.”

Mohamed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, told The Associated Press on Sunday that it was the U.S. that had reached out to the rebel group after its advancement toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
“We confirmed that we are not targeting the United States, or any other nation, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy,” al-Bukhaiti said. “And that remains the case.”

Bawazir warned it would be a mistake to accept assurances from a group that is “connected to a deviant state in the region,” referring to Iran, as it may be seen as legitimizing the Houthis. But he said Yemen was comfortable with the U.S. position.
“We do indeed discuss this particular issue very, very deeply,” he said.

title: Treasury yields surge to near 20-year high as oil jumps back above $103 per barrel
summary: Mortgage rates hit the highest point of Trump’s second term, driven by the surging yield on 10-year Treasury bonds.
story: The yields on U.S. Treasury bonds jumped Wednesday and oil prices rose, sending stocks tumbling as investors braced for the prospect of future Fed rate hikes.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond, which heavily influences consumer borrowing rates, especially mortgages, rose as high as 5.13%, its highest since 2007. Indeed, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate jumped to 7.26% on Wednesday, according to Mortgage News Daily. That’s the highest point since Jan. 13, 2025 — and of President Donald Trump’s second term.
The 10-year yield’s rise was its sharpest one-day jump since April 9, 2025, a week after Trump’s tariffs began roiling global markets, according to Dow Jones data.
Yields on five- and 30-year Treasury bonds also hit levels that had not been seen since before the 2008 global financial crisis.
Stocks fell in response to the rise in yields and oil prices. The Nasdaq Composite index ended the trading session down 1.13%, and the S&P 500 fell 0.75%. The Dow declined 352 points.
International Brent crude oil climbed 3.8% to end the day at $103.08 per barrel, while U.S. crude oil closed up 1.8%, at $92.16. The rise in oil prices snapped a streak of five days of declines.
Rising oil prices often translate into higher bond yields because of the effect higher energy costs can have on inflation more broadly.
Yields move higher
One of the primary drivers of Wednesday’s rise in bond yields was the release of new economic data that revealed rising inflation.
Yields rise sharply when Treasury bonds sell off.

“US business activity growth accelerated for a fourth successive month in September to reach the fastest rate for over five years,” S&P Global reported in its latest purchasing managers index reading.

“Firms’ input costs have meanwhile jumped in September at the steepest rate for four years, with fuel and transport costs spiking higher thanks to the rise in oil prices seen during the month, which will add further to the upward pressure on selling prices and inflation in the coming months,” said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Investors viewed the data as likely to increase the odds of multiple Federal Reserve interest rate hikes later this year and next. As of late Wednesday afternoon, market odds for a Fed rate hike in October were up to more than 70%.
One Fed policymaker signaled that he would be likely to vote in favor of another rate increase during the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting.
“Risks to achieving our inflation target have increased, while risks to the labor market have receded,” Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr said at a housing conference in Chicago.
“In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion,” he said.
Oil prices rise
Crude oil trading desks Wednesday were focused on the latest developments in the Iran war.

Tuesday, the price of oil fell sharply after Trump said U.S. officials were holding talks with Iranian representatives at the U.N. General Assembly. But hopes that the talks would produce tangible results were dashed by a new report Wednesday that a cargo vessel had been “struck by an unknown projectile” in the Strait of Hormuz.
Lying just off Iran’s southwestern coast, the strait, a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies, has been under a military blockade for seven months.
Trump further shook energy markets Tuesday when he said he supported a ban on U.S. exports of diesel fuel.
“Let’s not send out the diesel,” Trump told reporters at the U.N. “I’ve called for it within my people. I’ve been talking about it.”
Trump’s remarks sent European benchmark diesel futures higher by as much as 7% early Wednesday.
But experts and energy industry groups warn that a ban on diesel exports would spell even higher gas prices for Americans.
“Removing U.S. diesel from the market could instead result in reduced refinery runs, global economic damage and even higher U.S. prices,” the American Petroleum Institute said in a statement.
Trump’s energy secretary, Chris Wright, also said a ban would not help bring down prices.
“The blunt tool of banning diesel exports definitely doesn’t work,” he said Wednesday at an event in New York, according to Reuters.
Wright said at an event hosted by The New York Times later Wednesday, “Nobody wants a full blanket ban or zero exports of diesel.”
“That’s not being discussed,” he said.
Stocks tumble
Inflation-sensitive stocks, such as travel companies and large technology firms, were hit hardest by Wednesday’s reversal.

The S&P’s biggest sector loser was utilities, which includes many of the companies leading the AI data center boom. Higher interest rates could add billions of dollars to the cost of building AI infrastructure.
The consumer discretionary and real estate sectors were also notable decliners.

title: U.S. says China trade truce extended by 2 months
summary: The agreement extends the suspension of some tariffs as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit.
story: The United States and China have agreed to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire in November through Jan. 10, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday.
The announcement came after Bessent and China’s vice premier, He Lifeng, held an unscheduled meeting in Washington.

“We will extend what we call the ‘Busan Agreement’ — the economic détente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on Nov. 10 — that is going to be extended until Jan. 10,” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News Channel.
Bessent said it’s possible a larger economic package will be agreed upon by January. But it’s also possible to “just roll the current deal” and extend it further.
Trump welcomes Xi at Joint Base Andrews

“There are some deliverables that have not been perfect on the Chinese side, so we also want to see, now that we’ve sat down and told them our expectations, if over the coming months they can be more fulsome in enacting the agreement,” he said.
The announcement, a big win for economic stability in both countries, came only minutes after Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down to begin a multiday state visit to Washington.

Bessent also indicated that there could be further announcements in coming days from the Chinese delegation, including agreements to buy more American agricultural products and potential deals in the financial services sector.
Since Sunday, Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been holding talks with their Chinese counterparts to lay the groundwork for the closely watched state visit.
On Sunday, Bessent and Greer announced that the U.S. and China had proposed exchanging alerts about AI-related hacking incidents, especially those that concern national security.
The U.S. and China could also agree on lists of goods on which lower tariffs would be applied as part of President Donald Trump’s “Board of Trade” initiative with China, Greer told reporters.

“We expect that the types of goods you’ll see in those lists are consumer goods, low-tech items coming in from the Chinese side,” he said. “On the U.S. side, energy products, agricultural goods, potentially medical devices and other things like that.”
Xi’s trip is his first state visit to the U.S. in more than a decade.

News of the trade truce extension is likely to be widely welcomed in Washington and Beijing, given that the U.S. and China are vital sources of goods for each other and for their millions of consumers and businesses.

title: Iran’s president strikes a defiant tone at U.N. after Trump threats
summary: Masoud Pezeshkian’s appearance at the General Assembly was the first time the leader of a country at war with the U.S. has addressed the world body.
story: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian struck a defiant tone during his address at the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday, the first time the leader of a country at war with the United States has addressed the world body.

“America and Israel attacked us, equipped with the latest technology and weapon systems, and our people stood steadfast,” Pezeshkian said one day after President Donald Trump had threatened to “annihilate” Iran. “Yes, they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee, we did not bow our head.”
Pezeshkian vowed that Iran would not limit its nuclear program, which it maintains is for civilian purposes, while also saying it was open to negotiations.
“Iran’s defense, our defensive systems have been built so that no one can think that bombing of Iranian cities will go unanswered. That is why we have the military power we do for defense,” he added.
Pezeshkian also highlighted civilian casualties by holding up a picture of children killed when a U.S. munition likely hit an elementary school in Minab in southern Iran, NBC News has reported.

While the U.S. military has yet to directly accept the blame for the bombings on the first day of the war, experts commissioned by the U.N.’s top human rights body say they have found “reasonable grounds” to believe America committed war crimes in the strikes, which Iranian state media says killed 168 people, mostly children.
A U.S. representative at the U.N. walked out as Pezeshkian mentioned civilian casualties, and many seats were empty during his address.

Pezeshkian also displayed a photograph of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed when the Israeli military targeted his compound in Tehran on Feb. 28, alongside members of his family and senior Iranian officials.

“I don’t know what standing Iran has to lecture anyone on human rights or the international system when they habitually violate it,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters after the speech. “They violate the sovereignty of every one of their neighbors by sponsoring terrorist organizations that reside in the borders of those countries. They slaughter their own people.”
Pezeshkian’s address followed Trump’s speech Tuesday, during which the American president threatened to destroy Iran.

“I have a big decision to make,” Trump said. “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”
Despite his threat, Trump later told reporters that U.S. officials had a “very good meeting” with their Iranian counterparts Tuesday.
U.S. envoys held indirect talks with Iranian officials, and Qatari diplomats acted as intermediaries during that meeting, according to a Middle Eastern official with knowledge of the matter.

The Qatari diplomats conveyed questions and responses from U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner to the Iranian officials, who then relayed their answers back via Qatar, the official said.
“I don’t want to mischaracterize this as a major breakthrough, but at the same time I think it was significant that there was at least a conversation,” Rubio said Wednesday.
U.S. delegation walks out of Iranian president's speech
Pezeshkian also noted that further talks could be possible.
“Iran must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force,” he said.
Trump also said during his U.N. address that there would likely be a deal with Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November, though he did not provide any additional details.
Pezeshkian defended Iran’s right to continue with its civilian nuclear program.
“We say it clearly: no nuclear weapons and no limitations to new peaceful nuclear technology,” he said.

Trump has repeatedly said that the goal of attacking Iran was to prevent the development of a nuclear weapon, which Iranian officials have said for years that they are not pursuing. Soon after the war started, however, Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the conflict, sending shock waves through the world economy.
Iran and the U.S. signed a preliminary agreement, often referred to as a memorandum of understanding, in June aimed at ending the war and opening the strait.

But heavy fighting broke out again over the summer, with Iran striking U.S. allies throughout the region. This derailed the talks and left the strait largely closed to maritime traffic as Iran attacked ships and the U.S. imposed a naval blockade, which also included attacks on oil tankers.

The U.S. military announced the death of four American soldiers in July, and Iranian officials have said dozens of civilians have been killed in recent attacks on cities in southern Iran on the coastline of the strait.

Any discussions that take place between American and Iranian officials in New York will likely focus on the opening of the strait, according to Sina Azodi, director of the Middle East studies program at George Washington University.

“The main discussion will be over returning to the MOU, which is essentially lifting the blockade on Iran and Iran lifting the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz,” Azodi said, noting that gas prices have spiked in the U.S., and the Iranian economy has been squeezed by the U.S. naval blockade.

Before traveling to New York, both Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were under tremendous pressure from Iranian hard-liners not to hold any talks with U.S. officials. Some hard-liners see negotiations with the U.S. as a form of capitulation, and Pezeshkian and Araghchi is likely to face their wrath when they return.
Last year, the late Khamenei set the red lines for Pezeshkian prior to his trip to New York and said negotiating with the U.S. about the country’s nuclear program or other issues would be a dead end.
This year, his son and successor, Mojtaba Khamenei, does not appear to have publicly laid out any parameters for what the Iranian delegation may discuss with their American counterparts.

title: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
summary: In a speech to world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the Iran conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country and drive it “into hell.”
story: In a speech to world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the Iran conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country and drive it “into hell.”
Or, he said, Iran could make a deal with the U.S. that would allow the nation to rebuild. But that won’t happen until after the midterm elections in November, Trump predicted.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”
Trump later said U.S. envoys met with Iranian officials for three hours on the sidelines of the gathering, an unexpected development that offered a glimpse of diplomatic activity.

But Trump has repeatedly floated new attacks on Iran, even previously threatening death to the entire civilization. On Tuesday, he revived that warning at one of the most prominent platforms for world leaders, with an Iranian delegation in the audience.

“I have a big decision to make,” he said. “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”
“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he continued.
Most important, Trump said to applause, is ensuring that “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”

Iran’s nuclear potential was “the reality we had to confront,” he argued, and “a reality that far too many preferred to ignore.” Tehran has insisted its nuclear program is for civilian purposes and denied having plans to develop nuclear weapons.
The U.N. assembly comes as the Iran war is about to enter its eighth month.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the U.N. on Wednesday. Trump told Fox News that he would “probably” be open to meeting with Pezeshkian but did not announce any specifics.
